en: Not free to move.
Limited; narrow; restricted.

ex.en: He is confined to his house by illness.
ex.ja: 彼は病気で家に引きこもっている。

ex.en: A bad cold confined her to her bed.
ex.ja: 彼女はひどい風邪で床を離れることができなかった。

ex.en: Soccer is not necessarily confined to men.
ex.ja: サッカーは必ずしも男だけに限られたものではない。

note.ja: confine（閉じ込める）+ -ed。con（共に）+ finis（境界）。「境界の中に入れる」→「限られた・閉じ込められた」。finish、final と同じ fin。

en: The act of congregating or collecting together.
A gathering of faithful in a temple, church, synagogue, mosque or other place of worship, especially those present at a devotional servic…

congregation.ety: From Middle English congregacioun, from Old French congregacion, from Latin congregātiō, itself from congregō (“to herd into a flock”). Adopted (1520s) by the English Bible translator William Tyndale, to render the Ancient Greek ἐκκλησία (ekklēsía, “those called together, (popular) meeting”) (hence Latin ecclēsia) in his New Testament, and preferred by 16th century Reformers instead of church. By surface analysis, congregate + -ion.

ex.en: The congregation was moved by the fine sermon.
ex.ja: 会衆は素晴らしい説教に感動した。

ex.en: The church congregation was moved by the fine sermon.
ex.ja: 教会の会衆は素晴らしい説教に感動した。

ex.en: The priest blessed the congregation at the end of the mass.
ex.ja: 司祭はミサの終わりに会衆を祝福した。

note.ja: con（共に）+ grex（群れ）+ -ation。「群れを集めること」→「（教会の）会衆」。gregarious（群れを好む）、aggregate も同じ grex。

en: Having undergone consolidation.
Including financial data of the parent and all subsidiary companies.

ex.en: The two banks consolidated and formed a single large bank.
ex.ja: 二つの銀行が合併して一つの大銀行を作った。

note.ja: consolidate（統合する）+ -ed。con（共に）+ solidus（固い）。「固めて一つにする」→「統合された・連結の」。solid と同じ。

en: Of the same rank; equal.
A number representing the position of a point along a line, arc, or similar one-dimensional figure.
Something that is equal to another thing.
To place in the same order or rank.
To synchronize (activities).

coordinate.ety: From Medieval Latin coōrdinātus, perfect passive participle of coōrdinō (“arrange together”), from co- + ōrdinō, equivalent to co- + ordinate. See -ate (adjective-forming suffix) for more. See also ordain and ordinate.

ex.en: She coordinates the volunteers at the event.
ex.ja: 彼女はイベントでボランティアの調整役をしている。

note.ja: co（共に）+ ordinare（並べる）。「同じ順序に並べる」→「調整する・座標」。order と同じ ord。

en: A regular polyhedron having six identical square faces.
Any object more or less in the form of a cube.
To raise to the third power; to determine the result of multiplying by itself twice.
To form into the shape of a cube.
Used in the names of units of area formed by multiplying a unit of length by itself twice.

cube.ety:
From Old French cube, from Latin cubus, from Ancient Greek κύβος (kúbos).
Displaced Old English tæfel ("cube, die, game with dice or tables").

ex.en: Do you want some ice cubes?
ex.ja: 氷が欲しいの？

ex.en: Three cubed makes twenty-seven.
ex.ja: 3の3乗は27です。

ex.en: Cut the cheese into thin slices or into little cubes.
ex.ja: チーズは細くスライスするか小さくキューブ状にカットします。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kybos（さいころ）から。「立方体・3乗」。

en: The act of adorning, embellishing, or honoring; ornamentation.
Any item that adorns, enriches, or beautifies; something added by way of embellishment or ornamentation.

decoration.ety: From Latin decoratio: compare French décoration. Morphologically decorate + -ion.

ex.en: You've done a wonderful job on the interior decoration.
ex.ja: すてきな室内装飾になりましたよ。

ex.en: He studied interior decoration.
ex.ja: 彼は室内装飾を学んだ。

ex.en: The shopping arcade was covered with lots of paper decorations.
ex.ja: アーケード天井にたくさんの張りぼてが飾られてた。

note.ja: decorate（飾る）+ -ion。ラテン語 decus（飾り・美しさ）。「装飾・勲章」。decent（ふさわしい）と同系。

en: An edict or law.
The judicial decision in a litigated cause rendered by a court of equity.
To command, especially by a decree.

decree.ety: From Middle English decre, decree, from Old French decré (French décret), from Latin dēcrētum.

ex.en: I need to escape from this decree.
ex.ja: この定めから逃れないといけない。

note.ja: ラテン語 decretum（決められたこと）から。de + cernere（決める・分ける）。「法令・命令」。discern（見分ける）と同じ cern。

en: Done on purpose; intentional.
Formed with deliberation; carefully considered; not sudden or rash.
To consider carefully; to weigh well in the mind.
To consider the reasons for and against anything; to reflect.

deliberate.ety: Inherited from Middle English deliberat(e), borrowed from Latin dēlīberātus, perfect passive participle of dēlīberō (“to consider, weigh well”) (see -ate (adjective-forming suffix) and -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from dē- + *līberō / lībrō (“to weigh”)), from *libera / libra (“a balance”); see librate. Doublet of deliber.

ex.en: She deliberated over whether to go or stay.
ex.ja: 彼女は行くかとどまるかを熟考した。

ex.en: They are deliberating what to do next.
ex.ja: 彼らは次に何をすべきか熟考中である。

ex.en: She was deliberate in everything she did.
ex.ja: 彼女は何をするにも慎重であった。

note.ja: de（完全に）+ liber（量る）+ ate。ラテン語 librare（天秤で量る）から。よく量った →「故意の・慎重な・熟考する」。

en: To cause to despair.
To be hopeless; to have no hope; to give up all hope or expectation.
Loss of hope; utter hopelessness; complete despondency.
That which causes despair.

despair.ety: From Middle English dispeir, from Anglo-Norman despeir and Old French desperer (from Latin dēspērō, dēspērāre), or desesperer, from des- (“dis-”) + esperer (“hope”). See also desperate. Displaced native Old English ormōdnes (“despair”) and Old English ortrīewan (“to despair”).

ex.en: The leader gave up the plan in despair.
ex.ja: リーダーは絶望して計画を断念した。

ex.en: She was in despair when her husband died.
ex.ja: 彼女は夫が亡くなって絶望していた。

ex.en: The student gave himself up to despair.
ex.ja: その学生は自暴自棄になった。

note.ja: de（離れて）+ sperare（希望する）。「希望を離れる」→「絶望」。desperate も同じ。

en: A cash payment of money by a company to its shareholders, usually made periodically (e.g., quarterly or annually).
A number or expression that is to be divided by another.
To pay out a dividend.

dividend.ety: From Middle French dividende, from Latin dīvidendum (“thing to be divided”), future passive participle of dīvidō (“to divide”), by surface analysis, divide + -end.

ex.en: The bank has raised its dividend by 20%.
ex.ja: その銀行は二割増配ですよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 dividendum（分けられるべきもの）から。divide（分ける）。「分ける分」→「配当」。

en: Anything driven at random.
A mass of matter which has been driven or forced onward together in a body, or thrown together in a heap, etc., especially by wind or water.
To move slowly, especially pushed by currents of water, air, etc.
To move haphazardly without any destination.

drift.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *dʰreybʰ-der.
Proto-Germanic *drībaną
Proto-Indo-European *-tis
Proto-Germanic *-þiz
Proto-Germanic *driftiz

Middle English drift
English drift
From Middle English drift, dryft (“act of driving, drove, shower of rain or snow, impulse”), from Old English *drift (“drift”), from Proto-Germanic *driftiz (“drift”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰreybʰ- (“to drive, push”). Equivalent to drive + -t; cognate with North Frisian drift (“drift”), Saterland Frisian Drift (“current, flow, stream, drift”), Dutch drift (“drift, passion, urge”), German Drift

ex.en: Many people drift through life without a purpose.
ex.ja: 多くの人が目的なく人生を漂う。

ex.en: Waves of joy drift through my opened heart.
ex.ja: 喜びの波は解き放たれた私の心を漂う。

ex.en: The boat drifted about on the sea.
ex.ja: その船は海を漂流した。

note.ja: 古英語 drīfan（追いやる）から。drive と同じ。「（流れに）押し流される」→「漂う・漂流」。

en: A colorant, especially one that has an affinity to the substrate to which it is applied.
Any hue or color.
To colour with dye, or as if with dye.

dye.ety:
From Middle English deye, from Old English dēah, dēag (“color, hue, dye”), from Proto-West Germanic *daugu (“color, shade”), from *daugan (“to conceal, be dark”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewh₂- (“to smoke, raise dust, camouflage”).
Cognates
Cognate with Old High German tougan (“dark, secretive”), tougal (“dark, hidden, covert”), Old English dēagol, dīegle (“dark, hidden, secret”), Old English dohs, dox (“dusky, dark”). See dusk.

ex.en: She has been dyeing her hair black for years.
ex.ja: 彼女は何年も前から髪を黒く染めています。

ex.en: Tom wants to dye his hair pink.
ex.ja: トムって、髪の毛ピンクにしたいんだって。

ex.en: Have you ever dyed your hair?
ex.ja: 髪染めたことある？

note.ja: 古英語 dēag（色）から。「染料・染める」。die（死ぬ）と発音は同じ。

en: A person distinguished for their educational work, a teacher.

educator.ety: From Latin ēducātor. By surface analysis, educate + -or.

ex.en: As an educator, he believes every child can learn.
ex.ja: 教育者として、彼はどの子どもも学べると信じている。

note.ja: educate（教育する）+ -or。e（外へ）+ ducere（導く）。「（能力を）引き出す人」→「教育者」。produce、introduce と同じ duc。

en: The subatomic particle having a negative charge and orbiting the nucleus; the flow of electrons in a conductor constitutes electricity.

electron.ety:
Blend of electric + ion, coined by Anglo-Irish scientist George Stoney in 1891, changed by him multiple times from an earlier electrolion and original electrine (used as early as 1874) as the name for the electric charge associated with a univalent ion. Compare electro-, -on.
The particle ("corpuscule") was discovered in 1896. The name electrion was proposed for the particle in 1906 but curtailed because Hendrik Lorentz preferred electron.

ex.en: An electron is an elementary particle.
ex.ja: 電子とは素粒子の一種である。

ex.en: Atoms are composed of protons, neutrons, and electrons.
ex.ja: 原子は陽子・中性子・電子で構成されている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 ēlektron（琥珀）から。琥珀をこすると静電気が起きることから electric が生まれ、「電子」となった。

en: To continue or carry on, despite obstacles or hardships; to persist.
To tolerate or put up with something unpleasant.

endure.ety:
Etymology tree
Latin indūrō
Latin indūrāreder.
Old French endurerbor.
Middle English enduren
English endure
From Middle English enduren, from Old French endurer, from Latin indūrō (“to make hard”). Displaced Old English drēogan, which survives dialectally as dree. Doublet of dure.

ex.en: There are various ways of enduring the pain.
ex.ja: その痛みに耐えるさまざまな方法がある。

ex.en: I can't endure that noise a moment longer.
ex.ja: あの騒音にはもうこれ以上は我慢する事は出来ません。

ex.en: He has endured physical and mental pain.
ex.ja: 彼は肉体的、精神的苦痛に耐えてきた。

note.ja: en（中に）+ durare（固くする・続く）。「固く持ちこたえる」→「耐える」。durable、during と同じ dur。

en: A biomolecule that catalyses a biological chemical reaction: either a globular protein with this function or an RNA molecule with this fu…
The protein type specifically.

enzyme.ety: From German Enzym, coined 1878 by the German physiologist Wilhelm Kühne from Ancient Greek ἐν (en, “in”) + ζύμη (zúmē, “leaven”). By surface analysis, en- + zyme.

ex.en: This enzyme helps the body digest food.
ex.ja: この酵素は体が食べ物を消化するのを助ける。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 en（中に）+ zymē（酵母）。「酵母の中にあるもの」→「酵素」。

en: Of or relating to the biological theory of evolution.
Having formal similarities to the biological theory of evolution.

ex.en: Feathers were an important evolutionary step for birds.
ex.ja: 羽毛は鳥にとって重要な進化の一歩だった。

note.ja: evolution（進化）+ -ary。「進化の」。

en: A part broken off; a small, detached portion; an imperfect part, either physically or not.
A sentence not containing a subject or a predicate; a sentence fragment.
To break apart.
To cause to be broken into pieces.

fragment.ety: From Late Middle English fragment, from Latin fragmentum (“a fragment, remnant”), from frangō (“to break”) + -mentum.

ex.en: The glass bowl broke into tiny fragments.
ex.ja: ガラスの鉢は粉々になってしまった。

ex.en: Fragments of the mirror were scattered on the floor.
ex.ja: 鏡の破片が床に散乱していた。

ex.en: The vase broke into fragments.
ex.ja: 花びんは粉々になった。

note.ja: frag（壊す）+ ment。壊れたもの →「破片・断片」。

en: Synonym of geologic.

geological.ety: From Renaissance Latin geōlogia + -ical; first attested slightly earlier than geology. By surface analysis, geo- + -logical.

ex.en: Can you give me a geological explanation of lava?
ex.ja: 溶岩を地理学的に説明してくれませんか。

ex.en: That decision, in turn, was affected by the geological structure of the hill itself.
ex.ja: そうした決定は、今度は、丘そのものの地質的構造に影響される。

note.ja: geology（地質学）+ -ical。ギリシャ語 gē（大地）+ logia。「地質学の」。geography と同じ geo。

Over the entire planet.

ex.ja: その会社は製品を世界中で販売している。

en: In Indian traditions: a spiritual teacher who transmits knowledge to a shishya.
Any general teacher (as a term of respect).
To act as a guru; to give wise advice

guru.ety: Borrowed from Hindi गुरु (guru) / Punjabi ਗੁਰੂ (gurū), from Sanskrit गुरु (guru, “venerable, respectable”), originally "heavy" and in this sense cognate to English grieve and, more distantly, brute. Doublet of grave. A traditional, though flawed etymology based on the Advayataraka Upanishad (line 16) describes the syllables gu as “darkness” and ru as “destroyer”, thus ascribing the meaning of “one who destroys/dispels darkness” to the word.

ex.en: I have an appointment to visit a guru in India.
ex.ja: 私はインドのグルに会う約束があります。

note.ja: サンスクリット語 guru（重い・尊い・師）から。「師」→「指導者・第一人者」。

en: A horizontal door in a floor or ceiling.
A trapdoor.
To close with a hatch or hatches.

hatch.ety: From Middle English hacche, hache, from Old English hæċ, from Proto-West Germanic *hakkju (compare Dutch hek ‘gate, railing’, Low German Heck ‘pasture gate, farmyard gate’), variant of *haggju ‘hedge’. More at hedge.

ex.en: The crew is now opening the hatch.
ex.ja: 乗務員がただいま出入り口を開けております。

ex.en: Don't count your chickens before they are hatched.
ex.ja: 卵がかえる前にひよこの数を数えるな。

ex.en: Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
ex.ja: 取らぬ狸の皮算用。

note.ja: 「かえる」は中英語 hacchen から。「ハッチ（開口部）」は古英語 hæcc（格子戸）からで別語。

en: Any substance produced by one tissue and conveyed by the bloodstream to another to effect physiological activity.
A synthetic compound with the same activity.
To treat with hormones.

ex.en: Love is nothing more than a temporary hormone imbalance.
ex.ja: 恋とはホルモンバランスの一時的な乱れに過ぎない。

ex.en: Female hormone imbalance is a major cause of infertility.
ex.ja: 女性ホルモン分泌の乱れが不妊症の大きな原因です。

ex.en: If a woman masturbates, she will secrete female hormones and become more feminine.
ex.ja: 女性が自慰をすれば女性ホルモンが分泌され、女性らしさが出てきます。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 hormōn（刺激するもの）から。hormaein（動かす）。体の働きを刺激する物質として名づけられた。

A person who is inadequate.

ex.ja: 当大学では外国人留学生の受け入れ施設が十分でない。

ex.ja: 私はその仕事に向かないと思った。

ex.en: The chief pronounced that the technique was inadequate.
ex.ja: 所長はその方法は不適当だと断言した。

note.ja: in（否定）+ ad + equ（等しい）+ ate。必要に見合っていない →「不十分な・不適切な」。

en: Endlessness, unlimitedness, absence of a beginning, end or limits to size.
A number that has an infinite numerical value that cannot be counted.

infinity.ety: From Middle English infinite, from Old French infinité, from Latin īnfīnitās (“unlimitedness”), from negative prefix in- (“not”), + fīnis (“end”), + noun of state suffix -tās. By surface analysis, infinite + -ity.

ex.en: The numbers go on to infinity.
ex.ja: 数は無限に続く。

note.ja: in（否定）+ fin（終わり）+ ity。終わりがないこと →「無限」。infinite（無限の）。

en: A light fabric containing patterns of holes, usually built up from a single thread.
A cord or ribbon passed through eyelets in a shoe or garment, pulled tight and tied to fasten the shoe or garment firmly.
To fasten (something) with laces.
To interweave items.

lace.ety: From Middle English lace, laace, las, from Old French las, from Vulgar Latin *laceum, based on Latin laqueus. Doublet of lasso.

ex.en: Ireland is famous for lace.
ex.ja: アイルランドは刺繍で有名である。

ex.ja: 私は寝室にレースのカーテンを買った。

ex.en: I bought lace curtains for my bedroom windows.
ex.ja: 寝室の窓用にレースのカーテンを買った。

note.ja: ラテン語 laqueus（わな・輪縄）から。「ひも」→「靴ひも・レース」。lasso（投げ縄）と同系。

en: A girl or an unmarried young woman.
A maidservant.
Virgin.
Without offspring.

maiden.ety: From Middle English mayden, meiden, from Old English mæġden (“girl”), originally a diminutive of mæġeþ (“girl”) via diminutive suffix -en, from Proto-West Germanic *magaþ, from Proto-Germanic *magaþs. Equivalent to maid + -en.

ex.en: His maiden work established his reputation.
ex.ja: 彼は処女作で詩人として名声を確立した。

ex.en: What is your mother's maiden name?
ex.ja: お母様の旧姓は何ですか？

ex.en: What is your maiden name?
ex.ja: 旧姓は、何？

note.ja: 古英語 mægden（少女）から。「乙女」→「初めての（maiden voyage 処女航海）」。maid はその短縮。

en: An open area in a town housing a public market.
The space, actual or metaphorical, in which a market operates.

marketplace.ety: From market + place. Displaced native Old English ċēapstōw, literally "cheap-stow".

ex.en: The old marketplace is busy every morning.
ex.ja: その古い市場は毎朝にぎわっている。

note.ja: market（市場）+ place（場所）。market はラテン語 mercatus（取引）。

en: A mechanical, thin, flat flexible part that can deform or vibrate when excited by an external force.
A flexible or semiflexible covering or waterproofing whose primary function is to exclude water.

membrane.ety: Late Middle English, borrowed from Latin membrāna (“skin or membrane that covers parts of the body”), from membrum (“a limb or member of the body”) + -āna. Doublet of membrana.

ex.en: A thin membrane covers the cell.
ex.ja: 薄い膜が細胞を覆っている。

note.ja: ラテン語 membrana（膜・皮）から。membrum（体の一部）。member と同じ。

en: Of, relating to, or characteristic of metal.
Made of or containing metal.
A metallic color.

metallic.ety: From Latin metallicus, from metallum (“metal”), from Ancient Greek μέταλλον (métallon). Equivalent to metal + -ic.

ex.en: Why does blood taste metallic?
ex.ja: 血って、なんで金属の味がするんだろう？

note.ja: metal（金属）+ -lic。ギリシャ語 metallon（鉱山）から。「金属の・金属的な」。

en: The study of methods used in a field.
A collection of methods, practices, procedures and rules used by those who work in some field.

methodology.ety: From French méthodologie. By surface analysis, method + -ology.

ex.en: In order to overcome the data gap, I developed a simple methodology.
ex.ja: データギャップを打開するように簡単な方法論を開発した。

note.ja: method（方法）+ -ology（学）。method はギリシャ語 meta（後を追って）+ hodos（道）。「道筋の学」→「方法論」。

en: The change undergone by a word when used in a construction.
The result of modifying something; a new or changed form.

modification.ety: From Middle English modificatioune, from Middle French modification and its etymon Latin modificātiō (“a measuring”), from modificāre (“to limit, control, modify”); see modify. By surface analysis, modify + -ication.

ex.en: It is worth noting that Lander made the necessary modifications.
ex.ja: ランダーが必要な修正を施したことは注意する価値がある。

note.ja: modify（修正する）+ -ication。ラテン語 modus（尺度）+ facere（する）。「尺度に合わせること」→「修正」。mode、model と同じ mod。

en: A person who commits murder.

murderer.ety: From Middle English murderere; equivalent to murder + -er.

ex.en: We were filled with anger against the murderer.
ex.ja: 我々は殺人者に対する怒りで胸一杯になった。

ex.en: The others have to try and catch the murderer.
ex.ja: ほかの人はなんとかして、その犯人を捕まえなければなりません。

ex.en: The murderer was finally caught last night.
ex.ja: その殺人犯は昨夜ついに逮捕された。

note.ja: murder（殺人）+ -er。古英語 morthor（殺人）。mortal と同じ祖先 *mer-（死ぬ）。

en: To have a nap; to sleep for a short period of time, especially during the day.
To be off one's guard.
A short period of sleep, especially one during the day.

nap.ety: From Middle English nappen, from Old English hnappian (“to doze, slumber, sleep”), from Proto-West Germanic *hnappōn (“to nap”). Cognate with Old High German hnaffezan, hnaffezzan (whence Middle High German nafzen (“to slumber”) whence German dialectal napfezen, nafzen (“to nod, slumber, nap”)).

ex.en: A few hours nap will do you good.
ex.ja: 少し仮眠をとるといいですよ。

ex.en: He is taking a nap half the time.
ex.ja: 彼はたいていうたた寝をしている。

ex.en: He is always taking a nap at school.
ex.ja: 彼は授業中いつも居眠りばかりしている。

note.ja: 古英語 hnappian（うたた寝する）から。「昼寝・うたた寝」。

en: A silvery elemental metal with an atomic number of 28 and symbol Ni.
A coin worth 5 cents.
To plate with nickel.
To distribute airborne leaflet propaganda.

nickel.ety:
Etymology tree
Ancient Greek νῑ́κη (nī́kē)
Proto-Hellenic *lāwós
Ancient Greek λᾱός (lāós)
Ancient Greek Νῑκόλᾱος (Nīkólāos)bor.
Latin Nīcolāusbor.
German Nikolaus
German Nickelbor.
English nickel
Borrowed from German Nickel, first used in a text by the Swedish mineralogist Axel F. Cronstedt as an abbreviation of Kupfernickel (“a mineral containing copper and nickel”), from Kupfer (“copper”) + Nickel (“insignificant person, goblin”), originally nickname of Nikolaus (“Nicholas”), due to the deceptive silver colour of the relatively valueless ore. Compare cobalt as related to kobolds.

ex.en: Nickel is a hard, silver-white metal.
ex.ja: ニッケルは硬い銀白色の金属です。

ex.en: Then I'd take the nickel out.
ex.ja: それからニッケルを取るよ。

ex.en: A nickel is a five-cent coin.
ex.ja: ニッケルは５セント玉です。

note.ja: ドイツ語 Kupfernickel（銅の小鬼）の短縮。銅が採れると思ったら採れない鉱石を、鉱夫が小鬼のいたずらと考えたことから。

en: A daughter of one’s sibling, brother-in-law, or sister-in-law; either the daughter of one's brother ("fraternal niece"), or of one's sist…
A daughter of one’s cousin or cousin-in-law

niece.ety: From Middle English nece (“niece, granddaughter”), from Old French nece (“niece, granddaughter”) (Modern French nièce (“niece”)) from Late Latin neptia, representing Latin neptis (“granddaughter”), from Proto-Indo-European *néptih₂ (“granddaughter, niece”). Doublet of nift.

ex.en: To tell the truth, she is my niece.
ex.ja: 実を言うと彼女は私の姪です。

ex.en: These three pretty girls are all nieces of mine.
ex.ja: この３人の美しい少女はみな私の姪です。

ex.en: Mary isn't my daughter. She's my niece.
ex.ja: メアリーは私の娘じゃないですよ。姪っ子なんですよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 neptis（孫娘・姪）から古フランス語を経た語。nephew（甥）と同じ祖先。

en: Missed, unnoticed.

overlooked.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *úp
Proto-Indo-European *-er
Proto-Indo-European *upér
Proto-Germanic *uber
Old English ofer-
Middle English over-
English over-
English looked
English overlooked
From over- + looked.

ex.en: I hope it will be overlooked this time.
ex.ja: このたびはお見のがしくださったらと望んでおります。

ex.en: Our teacher often overlooked his name on the list.
ex.ja: 私たちの先生は、たびたび名簿にある彼の名前を見落とした。

ex.en: Mistakes like these are easily overlooked.
ex.ja: このようなミスは見逃しやすい。

note.ja: overlook（見落とす）+ -ed。over（越えて）+ look。「上を通り越して見る」→「見落とす」。「見渡す」の意味もある。

ja: 許す（Pardon?：もう一度言ってください）

en: Forgiveness for an offence.
An order that releases a convicted criminal without further punishment, prevents future punishment, or (in some jurisdictions) removes an…
To forgive (a person).
To refrain from exacting as a penalty.
Often used when someone does not understand what another person says.

pardon.ety: From Middle English pardonen, from Old French pardoner (modern French pardonner), from Late Latin perdōnāre, from per- + dōnāre, possibly a calque (if not vice-versa) of a Germanic word represented by Frankish *firgeban (“to forgive, give up completely”), from *fir- + *geban. Akin to Old High German fargeban, firgeban (“to forgive”), Old English forġiefan (“to forgive”). More at forgive.

ex.en: He asked our pardon for making a mistake.
ex.ja: 彼は間違った事を許して下さいと我々に謝った。

ex.en: Pardon me for being in this dress.
ex.ja: こんな格好でしつれいします。

ex.en: Pardon me, can you add another wine bottle please?
ex.ja: すみません、ワイン１本追加お願いします。

note.ja: par（= per 完全に）+ don（与える）。（罪を）すっかり与え許す →「許す・恩赦」。I beg your pardon.（もう一度言ってください）。

en: To successfully convince (someone) to agree to, accept, or do something, usually through reasoning and verbal influence.

persuade.ety: From Latin persuādeō (“to persuade”). Cognate to for, sweet.

ex.en: It is difficult for us to persuade him.
ex.ja: 我々が彼を説得することはむずかしい。

ex.en: I persuaded him to give up the idea.
ex.ja: 因果を含めてあきらめさせた。

ex.en: The doctor persuaded him to give up smoking.
ex.ja: 医者は彼を説得してタバコをやめさせた。

note.ja: per（完全に）+ suadere（勧める）。「すっかり勧めて納得させる」→「説得する」。dissuade（思いとどまらせる）も同じ。

en: A raised platform built from the shore out over water, supported on piles; used to secure, or provide access to shipping; a jetty.
A similar structure, especially at a seaside resort, used to provide entertainment.

pier.ety: Inherited from Middle English pere (“bridge pillar, breakwater”), borrowed from either Anglo-Norman pere (“stone”, from Latin petra) or Old French *piere (Old Northern French pire, from either Late Latin *petricus or pēra "satchel"); compare Medieval Latin pira.

ex.en: All at once the ship left the pier.
ex.ja: 突然船は埠頭を離れた。

ex.en: I'm staying at a hotel near the pier.
ex.ja: 埠頭の近くのホテルに泊まってるよ。

ex.en: There used to be a pier here.
ex.ja: 昔ここには桟橋があったんだ。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 pera（橋脚）から。「桟橋・埠頭」。

en: One who precedes; one who has preceded another in any state, position, office, etc.; one whom another follows or comes after, in any offi…
A model or type of machinery or device which precedes the current (or later) one. Usually used to describe an earlier, outdated model.

predecessor.ety: From Middle English predecessour, from Old French predecesseor (“forebear”), from Late Latin praedēcessor, from Latin prae- (“pre-”) + Latin dēcessor (“retiring officer”), from Latin dēcēdō (“to retire, to die”) (English decease).

ex.en: We like the present headmaster better than his predecessor.
ex.ja: 私たちは前の校長先生よりも今度の校長先生のほうが好きです。

ex.en: His background parallels that of his predecessor.
ex.ja: 彼の経歴は前任者のそれに匹敵する。

ex.en: His humble background parallels that of his predecessor.
ex.ja: 彼の庶民的な経歴は前任者のそれと似ている。

note.ja: prae（前に）+ decessor（去った人）。de（離れて）+ cedere（行く）。「前に去った人」→「前任者」。successor の反対。

en: A competition in the answering of questions.
A school examination of less importance, or of greater brevity, than others given in the same course.
To question (someone) closely, to interrogate.
To instruct (someone) by means of a quiz.

quiz.ety:
Attested since the 1780s, of unknown origin.
* The Century Dictionary suggests it was originally applied to a popular toy, from a dialectal variant of whiz.
* The Random House Dictionary suggests the original sense was "odd person" (circa 1780).
* Others suggest the meaning "hoax" was original (1796), shifting to the meaning "interrogate" (1847) under the influence of question and inquisitive.
* Some say without evidence it was invented by a late-18th-century Dublin theatre proprietor who bet he could add a new nonsense word to the English language; he had the word painted on walls all over th

ex.en: I can make nothing of this quiz.
ex.ja: このクイズは全然分からない。

ex.en: We had a history quiz this morning.
ex.ja: 今朝は歴史の小テストがあった。

ex.en: We enjoyed the quiz show on television last night.
ex.ja: 私たちは昨晩、テレビでクイズショーを楽しんだ。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。18世紀ごろからある語で、「からかい」→「質問」→「クイズ・小テスト」。

en: The amount of rain that falls on a single occasion
The occurrence of liquid precipitation, the fall of rain.

ex.en: What is the average rainfall for July here?
ex.ja: ここの７月の平均降雨量はどのくらいですか。

ex.en: The leaves are fresh after a rainfall.
ex.ja: 雨上がりの木の葉は生き生きとしている。

ex.en: We had a heavy rainfall last night.
ex.ja: 昨夜は激しい雨が降った。

note.ja: rain（雨）+ fall（降ること）。「降雨（量）」。snowfall も同じ作り。

en: Careless or heedless; headstrong or rash.
Indifferent or oblivious to danger or the consequences thereof.

reckless.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Germanic *rōkijaną
Proto-West Germanic *rōkijan
Old English rēċan
Proto-Indo-European *lewh₁-
Proto-Indo-European *lewHs-der.
Proto-Germanic *leusaną
Proto-Germanic *lausaz
Proto-Germanic *-lausaz
Proto-West Germanic *-laus
Old English -lēas
Old English rēċelēas
Middle English rekles
English reckless
From Middle English rekles, reckeles, rekkeles, (also recheles), from Old English rēcelēas (“reckless, careless, negligent”), equivalent to reck + -less. Cognate with West Frisian roekeleas (“reckless”), Dutch roekeloos (“reckless”), German Low German ruuklos (“careless”), Ger

ex.en: He gets a kick out of reckless driving.
ex.ja: 彼は無謀運転にスリルを感じる。

ex.en: The two men were arrested for reckless driving.
ex.ja: 無謀な運転で二人の男は逮捕された。

ex.en: Jim drove too fast, which was reckless.
ex.ja: ジムは猛スピードで運転したが、それは無謀だった。

note.ja: reck（気にかける）+ -less（〜がない）。「気にかけない」→「無謀な」。reckon（数える・考える）と同系。

en: The act of redeeming or something redeemed.
The recovery, for a fee, of a pawned article.

redemption.ety: From Middle English redempcioun, from Old French redemption, from Latin redemptio. Doublet of ransom. Displaced native Old English ālīesung, ālīesnes.

ex.en: The movie is a story of a man's redemption.
ex.ja: その映画はある男の救いの物語だ。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ emere（取る・買う）+ -tion。「買い戻すこと」→「償還・（罪からの）救い」。redeem、example と同じ emere。

en: To play again.
To display a recording of a previous event, especially multiple times.
An act or instance of replaying (of playing something, such as a game, again); a replaying of (something).
A repeat or subsequent playing of some or all of something which was previously broadcast or performed, or a playing of something which w…

replay.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-der.
Old French re-bor.
Middle English re-
English re-
Proto-West Germanic *plehan
Old English pleġan
Proto-West Germanic *plegō
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂ti
Proto-Germanic *-ōną
Proto-West Germanic *-ōn
Proto-West Germanic *plegōn
Old English plegian
Middle English pleyen
Proto-West Germanic *plegō
Old English plega
Middle English pleye
English play
English replay
From re- + play.

ex.en: I find myself being enthralled by her reaction each time I replay it.
ex.ja: リプレーする度に彼女の反応にいちいち萌えてしまいます。

note.ja: re（再び）+ play（再生する・試合をする）。「再生・再試合」。

en: The action or process of reviewing, editing and amending.
The action or process of reviewing something previously learned, especially one′s notes in preparation for a test or examination.
To provide with a new vision.

revision.ety: Borrowed from French révision, from Latin revīsiō.

ex.en: The revision of this dictionary took six years.
ex.ja: この辞書の改訂には６年かかった。

ex.en: It seemed obvious to me that the plan needed a few revisions.
ex.ja: その計画には明らかに、いくつか検討すべき点があるように私には思えた。

ex.en: He advocates a revision of the rules.
ex.ja: 彼は規則の改正を唱えている。

note.ja: re（再び）+ vis（見る）+ ion。見直すこと →「改訂・修正・復習」。

en: A distinctive smell.
A smell left by an animal that may be used for tracing.
To detect the scent of; to discern by the sense of smell.
To inhale in order to detect the scent of (something).

scent.ety: From Middle English sent (noun) and senten (verb), from Old French sentir (“to feel, perceive, smell, sense”), from Latin sentiō, sentīre (“to feel, sense”). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *sent- (“to feel”), and thus related to Saterland Frisian Sin (“sense”), West Frisian sin (“sense”), Dutch zin (“sense, meaning”), Low German Sinn (“sense”), Luxembourgish Sënn (“sense, perception”), German Sinn (“sense”). The -c- appeared in the 17th century, possibly by influence of ascent, descent, etc., or by influence of science.

ex.en: This wild rose gives off a sweet scent.
ex.ja: この野バラは甘い香りを放つ。

ex.en: This flower has a scent all its own.
ex.ja: この花は独特の香りがする。

ex.en: The police set a dog on the scent.
ex.ja: 警察は犬にその臭いをかがせた。

note.ja: ラテン語 sentire（感じる）から。（鼻で）感じ取るもの →「香り・におい・手がかり」。

en: A piece of such stone, usually cut into a rectangular shape, used as a tile for flooring, roofing, etc.; (uncountable) such tiles collect…
A piece of other material used as a roofing tile.
Having the bluish-grey colour of slate (noun etymology 1, noun sense 4).
To cover (a building, or part of a building such as a floor or roof) with slates (noun etymology 1, noun sense 1.1).
To appoint or designate (someone or something); also, to nominate or propose (someone or something); specifically (politics), to nominate…

slate.ety:
The noun is derived from Middle English sclate, slat, slate (“type of rock; roofing slate; writing slate”), from Old French esclate, a feminine form of esclat (“broken piece, shard”) (modern French éclat), from Old French esclater (“to break, shatter”), from Frankish *slaitijan (“to split, break”), from Proto-Germanic *slaitijaną, the causative of *slītaną (“to cut up, split”); further etymology unknown (see the Proto-Germanic entry for a discussion). Doublet of éclat and slat.
The adjective and verb are derived from the noun.

ex.en: Let's throw it away and start over with a clean slate.
ex.ja: ご破算にしよう。

ex.en: Let's scrap everything and start over again with a clean slate.
ex.ja: すべてを白紙に返そう。

note.ja: 古フランス語 esclate（かけら）から。「割れたかけら」→「粘板岩・石板」→ 石板に書く名簿 →「候補者名簿」。clean slate（白紙）。

en: An external phenomenon that has an influence on a system, by triggering or modifying an internal phenomenon; for example, a spur or incen…
Something external that elicits or influences a physiological or psychological activity or response, or that affects any of the sensory a…

ex.en: Light is the stimulus that causes a flower to open.
ex.ja: 光が刺激となって花が咲く。

ex.en: People tend to require strong stimuli.
ex.ja: 人々は強い刺激を求める傾向がある。

ex.en: The doctor says stimulus is needed for appetite.
ex.ja: 食欲には刺激が必要だと医者は言う。

note.ja: ラテン語 stimulus（牛を追う突き棒）から。「突くもの」→「刺激」。stimulate も同じ。

en: The time of day when the sun appears above the eastern horizon.
The change in color of the sky at dawn.
To phase in.

sunrise.ety: From Middle English sonne-rys, sunne ryse, equivalent to sun + rise. Compare Middle English son risyng, sunne rijsyng, sonne-rysing (“sunrise”, literally “sun rising”).

ex.en: The beauty of the sunrise was beyond description.
ex.ja: その日の出の美しさは言葉で表わせないほどだった。

ex.en: We got up early to see the sunrise.
ex.ja: 私達は日の出を見るために早起きした。

ex.en: I can't start my day without seeing the sunrise.
ex.ja: 朝日を見ないと1日が始まらないよ。

note.ja: sun（太陽）+ rise（昇る）。「日の出」。

en: A sudden transient rush, flood or increase.
The maximum amplitude of a vehicle's forward/backward oscillation.
To rush, flood, or increase suddenly.
To accelerate forwards, particularly suddenly.

surge.ety:
The verb is from Middle English ^((please verify)) surgen, possibly from Middle French sourgir, from Old French surgir (“to rise, ride near the shore, arrive, land”), from Old Catalan surgir, from Latin surgō, contraction of surrigō, subrigō (“lift up, raise, erect; intransitive rise, arise, get up, spring up, grow, etc.”, transitive verb), from sub (“from below; up”) + regō (“to stretch”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₃réǵeti (“to straighten; right”), from the root *h₃reǵ-; see regent. Doublet of source and sourd.
The noun is from the verb.

ex.en: I see a surge in loan growth.
ex.ja: ローンがふくらみそうな気配を見せていますね。

ex.en: It is expected that the tsunami surge will be ten meters or less.
ex.ja: 最大１０メートルの津波が押し寄せるとみられます。

note.ja: ラテン語 surgere（立ち上がる）から。sub（下から）+ regere（まっすぐにする）。「わき上がる」→「急増・高まり」。resurrection（復活）も同じ。

en: The name of the Latin script letter T/t.
Something shaped like the letter T.
To redirect output to multiple destinations.

tee.ety:
* From Middle English, from Old English te, from Latin tē (the name of the letter T).
* (computing): By analogy with a T-shaped pipe that sends fluids in two directions.

ex.en: He placed the golf ball on the tee.
ex.ja: 彼はゴルフボールをティーの上に置いた。

note.ja: ゴルフで球を置く小さな台。語源ははっきりしない。T シャツの tee は T を読んだもの。

en: Something serving as an expression of something else.
A keepsake.
Done as an indication or a pledge.
Perfunctory or merely symbolic; done or existing for appearance's sake, or to minimally comply with a requirement.
To betoken, indicate, portend, designate, denote
To betroth

token.ety:
From Middle English token, taken, from Old English tācn (“sign, symbol”), from Proto-West Germanic *taikn, from Proto-Germanic *taikną (“indicator, symbol, sign”), from Proto-Indo-European *deyḱ- (“to show, instruct, teach”) with Germanic *k rather than *h by Kluge's law.
Cognate with Scots takin, taiken (“token, sign”), Saterland Frisian Teken (“sign, symbol”), West Frisian teken (“sign, mark, symbol”), Dutch teken (“sign, indication, symbol”), German Low German Teken (“sign, symbol”), German Zeichen (“sign, token”), Danish tegn (“sign, token, character”), Swedish tecken (“sign, indication”),

ex.en: Give me five tokens, please.
ex.ja: トークンを５枚ください。

ex.en: This is a small token of my gratitude.
ex.ja: これはほんの些細な感謝の印です。

ex.en: He is guilty and by the same token so are you.
ex.ja: 彼は有罪であり君も同様に有罪である。

note.ja: 古英語 tācn（しるし）から。teach（示して教える）と同じ祖先。「しるし」→「記念品・代用硬貨・トークン」。

en: A violent wind in the form of a mobile, rapidly rotating, funnel cloud that has contacted the ground.
To sweep through something violently.

tornado.ety: From earlier English ternado, attested since the 1550s as a nautical term for a windy thunderstorm. From Spanish tronada (“thunderstorm”), from tronar (“to thunder”), from Latin tonō (“to thunder”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tenh₂- (“to thunder”). The o and r were reversed in English (metathesis) under influence of Spanish tornar (“to twist, to turn”), from Latin tornō (“to turn”).

ex.en: There was a tornado in the village.
ex.ja: 村に竜巻が起こった。

ex.en: The tornado destroyed the whole village.
ex.ja: 竜巻で村全体が破壊された。

note.ja: スペイン語 tronada（雷雨）が tornar（回る）の影響を受けた語。「竜巻」。

en: The soft light in the sky seen before the rising and (especially) after the setting of the sun, occasioned by the illumination of the ear…
The time when said light is visible; the period between daylight and darkness.
Pertaining to or resembling twilight; faintly illuminated; obscure.
Synonym of mesopelagic (“Describing the pelagic zone of the ocean between the photic epipelagic and the aphotic bathypelagic zones, chara…
To illuminate faintly.

twilight.ety:
PIE word

From Middle English twilight, twyelyghte, equivalent to twi- (“double, half-”) + light, literally ‘second light, half-light’. Cognate to Scots twa licht, twylicht, twielicht (“twilight”), Low German twilecht, twelecht (“twilight”), Dutch tweelicht (“twilight, dusk”), German Zwielicht (“twilight, dusk”). Compare Old English twēone lēoht (“twilight”).

ex.en: We find ourselves in the twilight of our civilization.
ex.ja: われわれの文明の黄昏に。

ex.en: There was eternal twilight in the place.
ex.ja: そこには消えることのない薄明かりがあった。

ex.en: The twilight came on.
ex.ja: 薄暮れが迫った。

note.ja: twi（2つの・あいだの）+ light（光）。「昼と夜のあいだの光」→「たそがれ」。twin、twice と同じ twi。

ex.ja: 日本経済は当時、前例のない好況にあった。

note.ja: ラテン語 vagina（さや）から。「膣」。

ex.ja: やっべ単語テストあんの忘れてた。

en: Stop (especially when commanding a horse or imitative thereof); calm down; slow down.
An expression of surprise.
To attempt to slow (an animal) by crying "whoa".

whoa.ety: Whoa (c. 1843) is a variant of woa (c. 1840), itself a variant of wo (c. 1787), from who (c. 1450), ultimately from Middle English ho, hoo (interjection), probably from Old Norse hó! (interjection, also, a shepherd's call). Compare German ho, Old French ho ! (“hold!, halt!”).

ex.en: Whoa, are you serious?
ex.ja: わ〜、マジで？

ex.en: Whoa, if we keep chatting, despite actually arriving early, we'll end up late!
ex.ja: おっと、せっかく時間前に来たのに、ダベッてたら遅刻しちまう。

note.ja: 馬を止めるときのかけ声から。「どうどう・おっと」。

ex.ja: 進んで責任を取るということは成熟の印である。

en: Having no worth or use; without value.

worthless.ety: From Middle English *worthles, from Old English weorþlēas (“worthless”), equivalent to worth + -less. Cognate with Dutch waardeloos (“worthless”), German wertlos (“worthless”), Swedish värdelös (“worthless”).

ex.en: A promise given under a threat is worthless.
ex.ja: 脅迫のもとになされた約束は無効だ。

ex.en: An eight-year-old car is almost worthless.
ex.ja: ８年間も乗った車はほとんど価値がない。

ex.en: She was cheated into buying worthless stock.
ex.ja: 彼女はだまされて価値のない株を買わされた。

note.ja: worth（価値）+ -less。「価値のない」。

en: A slick and light ship for making pleasure trips or racing on water, having sails but often motor-powered. At times used as a residence o…
Any vessel used for private, noncommercial purposes.
To sail, voyage, or race in a yacht.

yacht.ety:
Circa 1557; variant of yaught, earlier yeaghe (“light, fast-sailing ship”), from Dutch jacht (“yacht; hunt”), in older spelling jaght(e), short for jaghtschip (“light sailing vessel, fast pirate ship”, literally “pursuit ship”), compound of jacht and schip (“ship”).
In the 16th century the Dutch built light, fast ships to chase the ships of pirates and smugglers from the coast. The ship was introduced to England in 1660 when the Dutch East India Company presented one to King Charles II, who used it as a pleasure boat, after which it was copied by British shipbuilders as a pleasure craft for we

ex.en: You are welcome to the use of my yacht.
ex.ja: 君は私のヨットを自由に使ってよい。

ex.en: There are a few yachts on the calm sea.
ex.ja: 穏やかな海にヨットが二三浮かんでいる。

ex.en: Our yacht club has ten members.
ex.ja: 我々のヨットクラブは１０人のメンバーで構成されている。

note.ja: オランダ語 jacht（追跡船）から。jagen（狩る）。「速い船」→「ヨット」。ch は発音しない。

en: To include so that it no longer has separate existence; to overwhelm; to cause to disappear as if by swallowing up; to incorporate; to as…
To suck up; to drink in; to imbibe, like a sponge or as the lacteals of the body; to chemically take in.

absorb.ety: From Middle French absorber, from Old French assorbir, from Latin absorbeō (“swallow up”), from ab- (“from”) + sorbeō (“suck in, swallow”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *srebʰ- (“to sip”). Compare French absorber.

ex.en: I can't absorb all of the lesson in an hour.
ex.ja: 私は１時間ではその課を全部は理解できない。

ex.en: Work absorbs most of his time.
ex.ja: 彼は仕事に時間のほとんどをとられてしまう。

ex.en: This book is so absorbing that I can't put it down.
ex.ja: この本は興味津々たるものがあって飽きない。

note.ja: ab（離れて）+ sorbere（吸い込む）。「吸い込む」→「吸収する・夢中にさせる」。absorbed。

en: The act of advancing; promotion to a higher place or dignity
The state of being advanced

advancement.ety: From Middle English avancement, Old French avancement. See advance. Morphologically advance + -ment.

ex.en: The advancement of modern medicine was a long process.
ex.ja: 近代医学の進歩は長い道程を歩んだ。

ex.en: His poor educational background was not a bar to his advancement.
ex.ja: 貧しい学歴が彼の出世の妨げとはならなかった。

ex.en: Stop the enemy's advancement.
ex.ja: 敵の前進を止めよ。

note.ja: advance（前進する）+ -ment。ラテン語 abante（前から）。「前に進むこと」→「進歩・昇進」。

en: In an alternative way.
Used to link a pair of opposing possibilities.

ex.en: You can walk, or alternatively, I'll drive you there in my car.
ex.ja: 歩いても行けますが、代わりに私の車でそこまで送りましょう。

note.ja: alternative + -ly。「あるいは・代わりに」。alter（ほかの）と同系。

en: The act of assuring; a declaration intended to inspire full confidence; something designed to give confidence to someone.
The state of being assured; total confidence or trust; a lack of doubt; certainty; guarantee.

assurance.ety: From Middle English assuraunce, from Old French asseürance, from asseürer; as if assure + -ance.

ex.en: She had something of the assurance of a famous actress.
ex.ja: 彼女には有名な女優であるという自信が多少あった。

ex.en: She answered all the questions with assurance.
ex.ja: 彼女は全ての問題に自信を持って答えた。

note.ja: assure（保証する）+ -ance。ad（〜に）+ securus（安心な）。「安心させること」→「保証・確信・自信」。sure、secure と同じ。

A barber surgeon, a foot soldier specializing in treating battlefield injuries.
To cut the hair or beard of (a person).
(US, slang) To chatter, talk.

ex.ja: 月に一度、床屋に行きます。

en: To strike heavily; to beat.
To collide.
A forceful blow or impact.
A large party; a gala event.

bash.ety: From Middle English *basshen, *basken, likely from Old Norse *baska (“to strike”), akin to Swedish basa (“to baste, whip, lash, flog”), Danish baske (“to beat, strike, cudgel”), German patschen (“to slap”)

ex.en: I'm having a bash myself at the ballet.
ex.ja: 私の方はバレーで盛り上がっている。

ex.en: What a gorgeous bash!
ex.ja: すごいパーティーだなあ！

ex.en: The robber bashed her head in.
ex.ja: 強盗は彼女の頭をめった打ちにした。

note.ja: 擬音的な語。bang + smash とされる。「強く打つ」→「たたく（非難）」。

en: An army unit having two or more companies, etc. and a headquarters. Traditionally forming part of a regiment.
an army unit having two or more companies, etc. and a headquarters; forming part of a brigade.
To form into battalions.

battalion.ety: From Middle French battaillon (modern French bataillon).

ex.en: The battalion marched through the town.
ex.ja: その大隊は町の中を行進した。

note.ja: イタリア語 battaglione（大部隊）から。battaglia（戦い）。battle と同じ。

en: To abstain, either as an individual or a group, from using, buying, or dealing with someone or some organization as an expression of prot…
The act of boycotting.

boycott.ety: From Charles Boycott, an English evicting land agent in Ireland who was subject to a boycott organized by the Irish Land League in 1880. For the surname see Boycott.

ex.en: He organized a boycott of the bus service.
ex.ja: 彼はバスのボイコット運動を組織したのである。

en: A person skilled at carpentry, the trade of cutting and joining timber in order to construct buildings or other structures.
A senior rating in ships responsible for all the woodwork onboard; in the days of sail, a warrant officer responsible for the hull, masts…
To work as a carpenter, cutting and joining timber.

carpenter.ety:
From Middle English carpenter, from Anglo-Norman carpenter (compare Old French charpentier), from Late Latin carpentārius (“a carpenter”), from Latin carpentārius (“a wagon-maker, carriage-maker”), from Latin carpentum (“a two-wheeled carriage, coach, or chariot, a cart”), from Gaulish carbantos, from Proto-Celtic *karbantos (“chariot, war chariot”), probably related to Proto-Celtic *karros (“wagon”). Doublet of carpintero. More at car.
Displaced native Old English trēowwyrhta (literally “tree worker”).

ex.en: My father and my younger sister are carpenters.
ex.ja: 父と妹は大工さんです。

ex.en: All three of those men are carpenters.
ex.ja: あの男たち三人ともみんな大工です。

ex.en: My father and my sister are carpenters.
ex.ja: 父と妹は大工さんです。

note.ja: ラテン語 carpentarius（荷車職人）から。carpentum（二輪車）。「荷車を作る職人」→「大工」。

en: A characteristic manner or style of preparing food, often associated with a place of origin.
The food prepared using such style.

cuisine.ety: Borrowed from French cuisine (“cooking, culinary art, kitchen”), from Late Latin cocīna, from earlier coquīna (“kitchen”). Doublet of kitchen.

ex.en: This restaurant is famous for its excellent cuisine.
ex.ja: このレストランは料理がおいしいので有名だ。

ex.en: After 1639 Japan closed the door to foreign cuisine.
ex.ja: １６３９年以降日本は外国料理に対して門戸を閉ざした。

ex.en: Japanese eat more than just Japanese cuisine.
ex.ja: 日本人は和食ばかり食べているわけではありません。

note.ja: フランス語 cuisine（台所・料理）から。ラテン語 coquere（料理する）。cook、kitchen、cooker と同じ祖先。

en: Delayed or held back; kept from proceeding.
Held in custody or confinement.

ex.en: My boss detained me more than 30 minutes.
ex.ja: 上司は、私を３０分以上も引き留めた。

ex.en: Tom was detained by the police.
ex.ja: トムは警察に逮捕されました。

note.ja: detain（拘束する）+ -ed。de（離して）+ tenere（保つ）。「引き止められた」→「拘束された」。retain と同じ ten。

en: Destiny, especially terrible.
An undesirable fate; an impending severe occurrence or danger that seems inevitable.
To pronounce judgment or sentence on; to condemn.
To destine; to fix irrevocably the ill fate of.

doom.ety:
From Middle English doom, dom, from Old English dōm (“judgement”), from Proto-West Germanic *dōm, from Proto-Germanic *dōmaz, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰóh₁mos.
Cognates
Compare Dutch doem (“condemnation, doom; judgement”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish dom (“judgement”), Faroese and Icelandic dómur (“judgement”), Gothic 𐌳𐍉𐌼𐍃 (dōms, “insight, judgement”); also Ancient Greek θωμός (thōmós, “heap”), Bulgarian, Macedonian, Russian, and Ukrainian ду́ма (dúma, “thought”), Polish duma (“pride”). Doublet of duma. See also deem.

ex.en: The plan was doomed to failure from the start.
ex.ja: この計画は初めから失敗する事に運命付けられていた。

ex.en: He was doomed to life-long poverty.
ex.ja: 生涯、貧しいままで生きるのが彼の運命であった。

ex.en: The enterprise was doomed to failure.
ex.ja: その事業は失敗する運命にあった。

en: Having had the original soundtrack replaced with a synchronized translation.
Remixed.

ex.en: The town was dubbed "the city of flowers."
ex.ja: その町は「花の都」と呼ばれた。

note.ja: dub（〜と呼ぶ・吹き替える）+ -ed。「〜と呼ぶ」は古フランス語 aduber（騎士に叙する）から。「吹き替え」は double の短縮で別語。

Especially, an alignment whereby a planetary object (for example, the Moon) comes between the Sun and another planetary object (for examp…
Of astronomical or atmospheric bodies, to cause an eclipse.
To overshadow; to be better or more noticeable than.

eclipse.ety: From Middle English eclipse, from Old French eclipse, from Latin eclīpsis, from Ancient Greek ἔκλειψις (ékleipsis, “eclipse”), from ἐκλείπω (ekleípō, “to abandon, go missing, vanish”), from ἐκ (ek, “out”) and λείπω (leípō, “to leave behind”). Doublet of eclipsis. See also ellipse, ellipsis.

ex.en: An eclipse of the sun is a rare appearance.
ex.ja: 日食はまれにしか起こらない。

ex.en: Did you see the solar eclipse yesterday?
ex.ja: 昨日の日食見た？

ex.en: Did you see the eclipse yesterday?
ex.ja: 昨日の月食見た？

note.ja: ギリシャ語 ekleipsis（欠けること）＝ ek（外へ）+ leipein（去る）。「光が去ること」→「食」→ 影を薄くさせる。

An enjoyable state of mind; a feeling of satisfaction or delight from a situation.

ex.en: They added to the enjoyment of my life.

ex.en: Reading is a great enjoyment to him.
ex.ja: 読書は彼にとって大きな楽しみです。

ex.en: The music added to our enjoyment.
ex.ja: 音楽は私達の楽しみを増やしてくれた。

note.ja: en（〜にする）+ joy（喜び）+ -ment。「楽しみ・喜び」。

ex.ja: お客様、申し訳ございませんが、こちらのクーポンは有効期限が切れております。

ex.en: This can of beans is expired.
ex.ja: この豆の缶詰、消費期限が切れてるよ。

note.ja: expire（期限が切れる）+ -ed。ex + spirare（息をする）。「息を吐き切る」→「死ぬ・期限が切れる」。spirit と同じ spir。

en: The process of collecting money by requesting donations from individuals and businesses.
Relating to raising money (funds), particularly for charities.

ex.en: The school held a fundraising event for the new library.
ex.ja: 学校は新しい図書館のための募金イベントを開いた。

note.ja: fund（資金）+ raise（集める）+ -ing。「資金集め」。

en: To see or view (someone, or something tangible) briefly and incompletely.
To perceive (something intangible) briefly and incompletely.
Chiefly followed by of: a brief and incomplete look.
A faint or imprecise idea; an inkling.

glimpse.ety:
The verb is derived from earlier glimse (obsolete), from Middle English glimsen (“to dazzle; to glisten; to glance with the eyes”), possibly from Old English *glimsian, from Proto-West Germanic *glimmisōjan, from Proto-Germanic *glimō, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰley- (“to shine”). Doublet of glimmer.
The noun is derived from the verb.
Cognates
Dutch glimp (“glimpse”, noun)
Middle Dutch glinsen (modern Dutch glinsteren (“to glint, glitter, shimmer, sparkle; to glance”), glimmen (“to gleam, shine”))
Middle High German glimsen (“to glow, smoulder”), glinsen (“to glimmer, shine”)
Middle Low Germa

ex.en: I caught a glimpse of him from the bus.
ex.ja: 私はバスから彼をちらりと見た。

ex.en: I glimpsed the girl among the crowd.
ex.ja: 私は人込みの中でその少女をちらっと見た。

ex.en: I caught a glimpse of him in the crowd.
ex.ja: 私は人混みの中で彼の姿をちらりと見た。

note.ja: 中英語 glimsen（ちらっと光る）から。glimmer、gleam と同系。「ちらりと見えること」。

en: Made at home.
Made by oneself.

ex.en: I like homemade food.
ex.ja: 家庭的な料理が好きです。

ex.en: This is homemade jam.
ex.ja: これは自家製のジャムです。

ex.en: This jam is homemade.
ex.ja: このジャムは手作りなのよ。

note.ja: home（家）+ made（作られた）。「家で作った」→「手作りの」。

en: Behaving in a manner that shows honor; decent, having integrity.
Worthy of respect; respectable.
A politician or other person who bears the title of "honorable".

honorable.ety: From Middle English honourable, from Old French honorable, honurable, from Latin honōrābilis, from honōrō (“to honour”); cognate with Italian onorabile, Spanish honorable. By surface analysis, honor + -able. In this sense, largely displaced Old English ārfæst.

ex.en: I would prefer an honorable death.
ex.ja: むしろ名誉ある死を選びたい。

ex.en: You should do the honorable thing and resign.
ex.ja: 君は潔く辞任すべきだ。

ex.en: His behavior is always honorable.
ex.ja: 彼のふるまいはいつも立派だ。

note.ja: honor（名誉）+ -able。「名誉に値する」→「立派な」。

en: Caused by an agent that enters the host's body (such as a bacterium, virus, parasite, or prion); often, also, transmitted among hosts via…
Able to infect others; capable of transmitting pathogens.

infectious.ety: Borrowed from New Latin īnfectiōsus. By surface analysis, infect + -ious.

ex.en: Don't treat me like I am infectious.
ex.ja: ばい菌扱いするなよ。

ex.en: The infectious case was isolated from other patients.
ex.ja: その伝染病患者は他の患者から隔離された。

ex.en: Not all the infectious diseases are contagious.
ex.ja: あらゆる伝染病が移るとは限らない。

note.ja: in（中に）+ fect（作用する）+ ious。中に入り込んで作用する →「伝染性の・人にうつりやすい」。

en: Lower in rank, status, or quality.
Of low rank, standard or quality.
A person of lower rank, stature, or ability to another.
An inferior letter, figure, or symbol.

inferior.ety: Borrowed from Latin īnferior (“lower in situation or place”), comparative of īnferus (“below, underneath”).

ex.en: He is much inferior to me in English.
ex.ja: 彼は英語ではわたしよりずっと劣っている。

ex.en: You are my equal; not my inferior or superior.
ex.ja: あなたは私と対等で私より下でも上でもない。

ex.en: He is little, if at all inferior to you.
ex.ja: 彼はほとんどまったくといっていいほど君に劣ってない。

note.ja: ラテン語 inferus（下の）の比較級。「より下の」→「劣った」。superior（より上の）の反対。

en: Absence of justice; unjustice.
Violation of the rights of another person or people.

injustice.ety: From Middle English injustice, from Old French injustice, from Latin iniustitia. Equivalent to in- + justice. Displaced native Old English unrihtwīsnes.

ex.en: You must speak out against injustice.
ex.ja: 不正には抗議せざるをえない。

ex.en: Woman as I am, I shall stand up against any social injustice.
ex.ja: 私は女性だが、どんな社会的不正にも立ち上がる。

ex.en: Cry out against injustice!
ex.ja: 不正に対して反対の声を上げろ。

note.ja: in（否定）+ justice（正義）。「正しくないこと」→「不正・不公平」。

en: A polypeptide hormone that regulates carbohydrate metabolism (in various animals including humans).
Any exogenous preparation of this hormone for use as a medication.

insulin.ety: From Latin īnsula (“island”) (named for the islets of Langerhans, where insulin is produced) + -in.

ex.en: The insulin was making her fat.
ex.ja: インシュリンを打つので彼女は太っていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 insula（島）+ -in。膵臓の「ランゲルハンス島」から出るホルモンなのでこう名づけられた。peninsula と同じ insula。

en: An introduction.
The opening sequence at beginning of a film, television program, etc.
To introduce.

intro.ety: Clipping of introduction, from Latin intrōductiō (“lead-in, introduction”) – the abbreviation removes the second part of the compound; the first part ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁énteros (“inner, what is inside”). The demoscene sense comes from the fact that they were originally prepended to pirated copies of computer games.

ex.en: I love the guitar intro of this song.
ex.ja: 私はこの曲のギターのイントロが大好きだ。

note.ja: introduction の短縮。intro（中へ）+ ducere（導く）。

en: To start (a fire) or light (a torch, a match, coals, etc.).
To arouse or inspire (a passion, etc).
pregnant

kindle.ety: From Middle English kyndelen, from Old Norse kynda (“to inflame”), from Proto-Germanic *kundijaną.

ex.en: A small spark often kindles a large flame.
ex.ja: 小さな火花はしばしば大きな炎を起こす。

ex.en: Whoops! There aren't many live coals left! Go make some kindling would you?
ex.ja: おっと！火種が残りすくないぞ！薪割りしてくれ！

note.ja: 北欧語 kynda（火をつける）から。「火をつける」→（感情を）かき立てる。candle とは別語源。

en: The top or cover of a container.
An operculum or other lid-like cover.
To put a lid on (something).

lid.ety:
Etymology tree

Proto-Indo-European *-éyti

Proto-Indo-European *-om

Old English hlid
Middle English lid
English lid
Inherited from Middle English lid, lyd, from Old English hlid, from Proto-West Germanic *hlid, from Proto-Germanic *hlidą (compare Dutch lid, German Lid (“eyelid”), Swedish lid (“gate”)), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱlitós (“covered”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱley- (“to cov

ex.en: He found it impossible to lift the lid.
ex.ja: 彼はそのふたを持ち上げるのが不可能だとわかった。

ex.en: She took off the lid of the box.
ex.ja: 彼女は箱のふたを開けた。

ex.en: The lid of this box won't lift.
ex.ja: この箱の蓋はどうしても開かない。

note.ja: 古英語 hlid（ふた）から。「ふた」→ 目のふた →「まぶた（eyelid）」。

en: A landed estate.
The main house of such an estate or a similar residence; a mansion.

manor.ety: From Middle English maner, manour; from Old French manoir, from earlier maneir, from Latin manēre. Doublet of maenor.

ex.en: The family lived in an old manor in the country.
ex.ja: その一家は田舎の古い屋敷に住んでいた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 manoir（住まい）から。ラテン語 manere（とどまる）。mansion、remain と同じ。「領主の館・荘園」。

en: A piece of work that has been given much critical praise, especially one that is considered the greatest work of a person's career.
A work of outstanding creativity, skill or workmanship.

masterpiece.ety: From master + piece, a calque of Dutch meesterstuk or German Meisterstück (“masterpiece”). Piecewise doublet of maestropiece and masterstick. Compare also journeyman's piece.

ex.en: They are great masterpieces of European art.
ex.ja: それらはヨーロッパ芸術の偉大な傑作だ。

ex.en: The plan was a masterpiece of fraud.
ex.ja: その計画は実にうまく考えた詐欺だった。

ex.en: His masterpiece has not appeared yet.
ex.ja: 彼の傑作はまだ現れていない。

note.ja: master（親方）+ piece（作品）。ギルドで職人が親方になるために提出した作品 →「傑作」。

en: A sequence of notes that makes up a musical phrase.

melody.ety: From Middle English melodie, melodye, from Old French melodie, from Latin melodia, from Ancient Greek μελῳδίᾱ (melōidíā, “singing, chanting”), from μέλος (mélos, “musical phrase”) + ἀοιδή (aoidḗ, “song”), contracted form ᾠδή (ōidḗ).

ex.en: I tried to learn the melody by heart.
ex.ja: 私は曲を覚えようとした。

ex.en: Their sweet melody made young people feel free.
ex.ja: 若者は彼らの甘いメロディーを聴いて自由な気持ちになった。

ex.en: I can't remember the melody to that song.
ex.ja: 私はあの歌のメロディーが思い出せない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 melōidia ＝ melos（歌の節）+ ōidē（歌）。ode（頌歌）、parody も同じ ōidē。

en: A short note; a memorandum.
A record of partial results that can be reused later without recomputation.
To record something; to make a note of something.
To send someone a note about something, for the record.

ex.en: Where has that memo got to?
ex.ja: あのメモはどこにあるのですか。

ex.en: I put a memo on my calendar.
ex.ja: 私はカレンダーにメモする。

ex.en: This is a memo.
ex.ja: これは備忘録です。

note.ja: memorandum（覚えておくべきこと）の短縮。ラテン語 memorare（思い出させる）。memory と同じ。

en: A microfarad.

ex.en: Tom's personality changes completely when he grabs the mic.
ex.ja: トムはマイクを握ると人格が変わる。

note.ja: microphone の短縮。micro（小さい）+ phone（音）。小さな音を拾う装置。

en: One who narrates or tells stories.
The person or the "voice" whose viewpoint is used in telling a story.

narrator.ety: From narrate + -or, from Latin narrātor. By surface analysis, Latin narr- + -ate + -or.

ex.en: The narrator of the story is a young girl.
ex.ja: その物語の語り手は少女だ。

note.ja: narrate（語る）+ -or。ラテン語 narrare（語る）、gnarus（知っている）。「知っていることを語る人」→「語り手」。

en: The state of being obese.

obesity.ety: From French obésité, from Latin obēsitās, from obēsus (“fat”). By surface analysis, obese + -ity.

ex.en: I suffer from obesity.
ex.ja: 肥満で困っています。

note.ja: ラテン語 obesus（食べて太った）から。ob（すっかり）+ edere（食べる）。「食べすぎた」→「肥満」。edible（食べられる）と同じ ed。

en: An adherent to a party or faction.
A fervent, sometimes militant, supporter or proponent of a party, cause, faction, person, or idea.
Serving as commander or member of a body of detached light troops.
Adherent to a party or faction; especially, having the character of blind, passionate, or unreasonable adherence to a party.

partisan.ety:
From French partisan, from Italian partigiano (“defender of a party”), from parte (“part”). Doublet of partigiano. Attested in English from the late 15th century in the noun sense of "party adherent", and in related adjective senses from the 16th century. The "guerrilla fighter" sense influenced by Serbo-Croatian partizan, Russian партиза́н (partizán), from the same source.
The sense of "guerrilla fighter" is from c. 1690.
The adjective in the military sense dates from the early 18th century.

ex.en: The debate became too partisan to be useful.
ex.ja: その議論は党派的になりすぎて役に立たなくなった。

note.ja: イタリア語 partigiano（党派の人）から。parte（部分・党）。「党派的な」→ 抵抗運動の「パルチザン」。part と同じ。

en: A small horse; specifically, any of several small breeds of horse under 14.2 hands at the withers.
A horse of any size.
To lead (a horse) from another horse.
To use a crib or cheat-sheet in translating.

pony.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *pel-
Proto-Indo-European *pelh₂-
Proto-Indo-European *polH-on-
Proto-Italic *polnos?
Proto-Indo-European *peh₂w-?
Proto-Indo-European *put-der.?
Latin pullus
Late Latin pullanus
Old French poulenetder.?
Scots powny
English pony
From Scots powny, apparently from Middle French poulenet (“little foal”), ultimately from Late Latin pullanus (“young of an animal”), from pullus. First attested in 1659. Doublet of foal and pullus.
Sense “small serving of alcohol” from 19th century, both for small sizes generally and for a quarter pint specifically, from the small si

ex.en: What's the difference between a horse and a pony?
ex.ja: 馬とポニーって、何が違うの？

note.ja: スコットランド語 powny（小さな馬）から。ラテン語 pullus（若い動物）とされる。poultry、foal と同系。

en: Lengthy in duration; extended; protracted.

ex.en: The session will be prolonged again.
ex.ja: 会期は又延長されるであろう。

ex.en: The stock market is in a prolonged slump.
ex.ja: 株式市場は長い不振を続けている。

ex.en: There followed a prolonged silence.
ex.ja: その後長い沈黙が続いた。

note.ja: prolong（長引かせる）+ -ed。pro（前へ）+ longus（長い）。「前へ長くのばす」→「長引いた」。long と同じ。

en: A reduction in consumer cost for a limited time for items or services rendered; a special.

ex.en: I saw a promo for the new show on TV.
ex.ja: テレビで新番組の宣伝を見た。

note.ja: promotion の短縮。pro（前へ）+ movere（動かす）。

en: Protesting.
One who protests; a protester.

protestant.ety: See Protestant. The legal sense either has the same source or is simply protest + -ant.

ex.en: This attitude, the Protestant work ethic, still influences Americans today.
ex.ja: 新教徒の労働観であるこの考え方は依然、今日のアメリカ人にも影響を与えている。

note.ja: protest（抗議する）+ -ant。16世紀の宗教改革でカトリックに「抗議した人々」→「プロテスタント」。

en: The act of relying (on or in someone or something); trust.
The condition of being reliant or dependent.

reliance.ety:
Etymology tree
English rely
Proto-Indo-European *-onts
Latin -ns
Latin -āns
Proto-Indo-European *-(i)yós

Latin -ius
Latin -ia
Latin -āntia
Old French -ancebor.
Middle English -aunce
English -ance
English reliance
From rely + -ance.

ex.en: Our reliance on smartphones keeps growing.
ex.ja: 私たちのスマートフォンへの依存は高まり続けている。

note.ja: rely（頼る）+ -ance。re（強く）+ ligare（結ぶ）。「固く結びつく」→「頼る・依存」。religion（神と結ぶ）と同じとされる。

en: Not wanting to take some action; unwilling to do something.
Tending to match as little text as possible.

reluctant.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin reluctāns (whence -ant), present participle of reluctor (“to struggle against, oppose, resist”), from re- (“back”) + luctor (“to struggle”) (whence re-.

ex.en: More Japanese are reluctant to have a child.
ex.ja: 子供の持ちたがらない日本人が増えている。

ex.en: He is reluctant to go to the college.
ex.ja: 彼は大学へ行きたがらない。

ex.en: I am reluctant to tell her the truth.
ex.ja: 彼女に真実を伝える気がしない。

note.ja: re（逆らって）+ luctari（もがく）+ -ant。「抵抗してもがいている」→「気が進まない」。

en: Relating to respiration or the organs of respiration; breathing.

respiratory.ety: Borrowed from New Latin respīrātōrius, equal to respire + -atory.

ex.en: Concerning the characteristics of respiratory function in swimmers.
ex.ja: 泳者の呼吸機能の特性について。

note.ja: respiration（呼吸）+ -ory。re + spirare（息をする）。「呼吸の」。

en: The act of retaining or something retained.
The act or power of remembering things.

retention.ety: From Middle English retencioun, borrowed from Latin retentiō, retentiōnis, from retentus, the perfect passive participle of retineō (“retain”) (from re- (“back, again”) + teneō (“hold, keep”)).

ex.en: Reviewing often helps the retention of new words.
ex.ja: 何度も復習すると新しい単語を覚えておきやすくなる。

note.ja: re（後ろに）+ tent（保つ）+ ion。保ち続けること →「保持・維持・記憶力」。retain（保持する）。

en: A long, narrow strip of material used for decoration of clothing or the hair or gift wrapping.
An awareness ribbon.
To decorate with ribbon.
To stripe or streak.

ribbon.ety: From Middle English riban, ryban, ryband, from Old French riban, ruban ( > modern French ruban), of uncertain origin. Likely from a Germanic compound whose second element is cognate with English band. Compare Middle Dutch ringhband (“necklace”, literally “ring-band”).

ex.en: The cat had a ribbon around its neck.
ex.ja: その猫は首にリボンを巻いていました。

ex.en: Jane had a yellow ribbon in her hair.
ex.ja: ジェーンは髪に黄色いリボンをしていた。

ex.en: Mary has a red ribbon in her hair.
ex.ja: メアリーは赤いリボンを髪につけている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 riban から。語源ははっきりしない。

en: A person with whom one shares a room, as in a dormitory, barracks, rooming house, or apartment.
A person sharing the same home albeit not the same room (but generally not a family member or spouse).

roommate.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *(H)rewH-der.

From room + -mate.

ex.en: Tom, my roommate, is a very nice guy.
ex.ja: ルームメイトのトムって、すごいいい奴なんだ。

ex.en: Tom, my roommate is a very nice guy.
ex.ja: トム、僕のルームメイトって、すごいいい奴なんだよ。

ex.en: We stayed roommates for four years.
ex.ja: 私たちは４年間ルームメイトだった。

note.ja: room（部屋）+ mate（仲間）。「同じ部屋の仲間」。classmate、teammate と同じ作り。

en: Of perishable items, overridden with bacteria and other infectious agents.
In a state of decay.
To an extreme degree.

rotten.ety: From Middle English roten, from Old Norse rotinn (“decayed, rotten”), past participle of an unrecorded verb related to Old Norse rotna (“to rot”) and Old English rotian (“to rot”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *rutāną (“to rot”). See rot. By surface analysis, rot + -en (past participle).

ex.en: Since it was rotten, it was thrown away.
ex.ja: 腐ってたから捨てたよ。

ex.en: The building is rotten inside and out.
ex.ja: その建物は内外ともぼろぼろになっている。

ex.en: Half of the apple was rotten.
ex.ja: そのりんごの半分は腐っていた。

note.ja: 北欧語 rotinn（腐った）から。rot（腐る）の過去分詞形。「腐った」→「ひどい」。

en: A gun which fires loads typically consisting of small metal balls, called shot, from a cartridge.
A one-story dwelling with no hallways or corridors, with the rooms arranged in a straight line.
To verbally lay claim to (something)
To hit the ball directly back at the pitcher.

shotgun.ety: From shot + gun. Front passenger seat sense comes from ride shotgun.

ex.en: Tom and Mary had a shotgun wedding.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは、できちゃった婚なのよ。

ex.en: He got in with a shotgun in his hands.
ex.ja: 彼は散弾銃を手にして乗り込んで来た。

ex.en: The hunter aimed a shotgun at the flock of birds.
ex.ja: ハンターは猟銃をその鳥の群れに向けた。

note.ja: shot（散弾）+ gun（銃）。「散弾銃」。shotgun（助手席）という俗語は、昔の駅馬車で銃を持って御者の隣に座った護衛から。

en: An upholstered seat with a raised back and one or two raised ends, long enough to comfortably accommodate two or more people.
To furnish with one or more sofas.
To seat or lay down on a sofa.

sofa.ety: Borrowed from French sofa, ultimately from Arabic صُفَّة (ṣuffa, “a long seat made of stone or brick, covered with rich carpets and cushions and used for sitting”). Cognate with Aramaic צפא/Classical Syriac ܨܦܬܐ (ṣipā’, ṣeppəṯā, “mat, matting”). The word may have entered European languages via Muslim Iberia or through Turkish.

ex.en: Sit on the sofa and make yourself comfortable.
ex.ja: ソファーに座ってくつろいで下さい。

ex.en: That sofa is less expensive than this table.
ex.ja: あのソファーはこのテーブルほど高価ではない。

ex.en: He lay on a sofa, his eyes closed.
ex.ja: 彼は目を閉じてソファーに横になっていた。

note.ja: アラビア語 ṣuffa（長いす・壇）からトルコ語・フランス語を経た語。

en: To ruin; to damage in such a way as to make undesirable or unusable.
To ruin the character of, by overindulgence; to coddle or pamper to excess.
Plunder taken from an enemy or victim.
Material (such as rock or earth) removed in the course of an excavation, or in mining or dredging. Tailings. Such material could be utili…

From Middle English spoilen, spuylen, borrowed from Old French espoillier, espollier, espuler, from Latin spoliō, spoliāre (“pillage, ruin, spoil”).

ex.en: A child is spoiled by too much attention.
ex.ja: あまり大事にすると子供はわがままになってしまう。

ex.en: As long as it doesn't spoil the weekend!
ex.ja: 週末が台無しになりさえしなければいいですよ。

ex.en: They were spoiled, as might have been expected.
ex.ja: 予想されたとおり彼らは甘やかされた。

note.ja: ラテン語 spoliare（はぎ取る・略奪する）から。spolia（戦利品）。「奪う」→「台なしにする・甘やかす・腐る」。

en: Being, relating to, or made for use underwater, especially beneath the sea.
Hidden or undisclosed.
A boat that can go underwater.
A pitch delivered with an underhand motion.
To operate or serve on a submarine.
To torpedo; to destroy with a sudden sneak attack.

ex.ja: 私はこれまで黄色い潜水艦を見たことがない。

en: A residential area located on the outskirts of a city or large town that usually includes businesses that cater to its residents; such as…
The outer part; the environment.

suburb.ety: From Old French suburbe, subburbe, from Latin suburbium (from sub- (“under-”) + urbs (“city”)). Displaced native Old English underburg (literally “underborough”).

ex.en: They decided to settle in a suburb of London.
ex.ja: 彼らはロンドン郊外に居を構えることに決めた。

ex.en: The other day something horrible happened in a Tokyo suburb.
ex.ja: 先日、東京の郊外で何か恐ろしいことが起こった。

ex.en: I have to commute all the way from a distant suburb.
ex.ja: 私は遠い郊外からわざわざ通勤しなくてはいけない。

note.ja: sub（下の・近くの）+ urb（都市）。都市のすぐそば →「郊外」。urban（都市の）。

en: Of, related to, feeling, showing, or characterized by sympathy.
Showing approval of or favor towards an idea or action.
A sympathetic nerve.

sympathetic.ety: Mid 17th century in the sense “relating to an affinity or paranormal influence”, from Latin sympathēticus. By surface analysis, sympathy + -etic (“pertaining to”); compare pathetic. Displaced native Old English efnþrōwiende.

ex.en: The girl and her parents were very sympathetic.
ex.ja: 少女と両親はとても思いやりがあった。

ex.en: A good doctor is sympathetic to his patients.
ex.ja: 良い医者は患者に同情を示す。

ex.en: The girl, like her parents, was very sympathetic.
ex.ja: 両親同様に少女も大変思いやりがあった。

note.ja: sympathy（同情）+ -etic。ギリシャ語 syn（共に）+ pathos（感情）。「同情的な」。

en: The act of imposing taxes and the fact of being taxed.
A particular system of taxing people or companies

taxation.ety:
From Middle English taxacioun, from Anglo-Norman taxacion, from Latin taxātio (“rating, appraisal”).
By surface analysis, tax + -ation.

ex.en: The people did not reach consensus on taxation.
ex.ja: 国民は税制に関しては意見が一致しなかった。

ex.en: Taxation is based on income.
ex.ja: 税金は収入に基づく。

ex.en: The people groaned under the burden of heavy taxation.
ex.ja: 国民は重税に苦しんだ。

note.ja: tax（税）+ -ation。「課税・税制」。tax はラテン語 taxare（評価する）。

en: A general tendency or orientation towards a certain type of mood, a volatile state; a habitual way of thinking, behaving or reacting.
State of mind; mood.
To moderate or control.
To strengthen or toughen a material, especially metal, by heat treatment; anneal.

temper.ety: From Middle English temperen, tempren, from Old English ġetemprian, temprian, borrowed from Latin temperō (“(transitive) to divide or proportion duly, to moderate, to regulate; (intransitive) to be moderate, temperate”), from tempus (“time, fit season”). Compare also French tempérer. Doublet of tamper. See temporal.

ex.en: There is no advantage in losing your temper.
ex.ja: かんしゃくを起こしても何の得もない。

ex.en: You have caused me to lose my temper.
ex.ja: お前のせいで私はかんしゃくを起こした。

ex.en: He lost his temper and threw a cup.
ex.ja: 彼は、かんしゃくを起こしてコップを投げた。

note.ja: ラテン語 temperare（適度に混ぜる）から。（気性を）ほどよく混ぜたもの →「気質・機嫌・かんしゃく」。temperature（温度）も同じ。

en: To experience; to pass through a phase.
To suffer or endure; bear with.

undergo.ety: From Middle English undergon, from Old English undergān (“to undergo, undermine, ruin”), equivalent to under- + go. Cognate with Dutch ondergaan (“to undergo, perish, sink”), German untergehen (“to perish, sink, undergo”), Swedish undergå (“to undergo, go through”).

ex.en: My father is going to undergo an operation.
ex.ja: 父は手術を受ける事になっている。

ex.en: This town has undergone a rapid change.
ex.ja: この街は急激な変化を遂げた。

ex.en: The new engine must undergo all the necessary tests.
ex.ja: 新しいエンジンは必要なテストをすべて受けなければならない。

note.ja: under（下で）+ go（行く）。「〜の下をくぐる」→「経験する・受ける」。

en: Any of the bivalve molluscs in the genus Venus or family Veneridae.

venus.ety: From translingual Venus (“a genus of clams”), from Latin.

ex.en: Is it possible to see Venus tonight?
ex.ja: 今夜は金星を見ることが可能ですか。

ex.en: Venus is a hot planet.
ex.ja: 金星は熱い惑星である。

ex.en: Venus is similar in size to Earth. Earth is just a little bit bigger.
ex.ja: 金星は地球と同じような大きさだけど、地球の方がほんの少し大きいよ。

note.ja: ローマ神話の愛と美の女神ウェヌス（Venus）から。「金星」。venerate（敬う）と同系。

en: Having been placed, arranged or formed in alignment (with something).
Allied or working together with a common goal.

ex.en: They aligned themselves with the Liberals.
ex.ja: 彼らは自由党員たちと同盟した。

note.ja: align（一列に並べる）+ -ed。フランス語 à ligne（線に）。「そろった・提携した」。line と同じ。

en: A table or similar flat-topped structure used for religious rites.
A raised area around an altar in a church; the sanctuary.

altar.ety: Inherited from Middle English auter, inherited from Old English altar and borrowed from Old French auter, both derived from Latin altāre, probably related to adolere (“burn”); thus "burning place", influenced by altus (“high”). Displaced native Middle English wēved.

ex.en: The couple stood before the altar.
ex.ja: 二人は祭壇の前に立った。

note.ja: ラテン語 altare（祭壇）から。altus（高い）とされる。「高くした所」→「祭壇」。altitude と同じ alt。

en: A bound collection of maps often including tables, illustrations or other text.
A bound collection of tables, illustrations, etc. on any given subject.

atlas.ety: Borrowed from Latin Atlas, from the name of the Ancient Greek mythological figure Ἄτλας (Átlas, “Bearer (of the Heavens)”), from τλῆναι (tlênai, “to suffer”, “to endure”, “to bear”). The sense referring to books of maps comes from the Atlas of Mercator, which he named thus in honor of Atlas, who was supposed to be skillful in astronomy and the doctrine of the sphere. The sense referring to the vertebra reflects that the spine carries the globe of the cranium (the neck carries the head).

ex.en: Open your atlas of Japan to page 3.
ex.ja: 日本地図の３ページを開けなさい。

ex.en: I paid 2,000 yen for this atlas.
ex.ja: 私はこの地図に2,000円払った。

note.ja: ギリシャ神話で天を担ぐ巨人アトラス（Atlas）から。16世紀の地図帳の表紙にアトラスが描かれたことから「地図帳」。

en: Of, from, or pertaining to Austria.
Of or pertaining to its people or their cultures.
A native or inhabitant of Austria.
An economist supporting the ideals of the Austrian School of Economics.

en: A feeling of fear and reverence.
A feeling of amazement.
To inspire fear and reverence in.
To control by inspiring dread.

awe.ety: From Middle English aw, awe, agh, awȝe, borrowed from Old Norse agi, from Proto-Germanic *agaz (“terror, dread”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂egʰ- (“to be upset, afraid”). ex.ja: 将軍の堂々とした恰幅は誰でも威圧される。

ex.ja: 彼らは教会内での厳粛な儀式を畏敬の念をもって見守った。

ex.en: With deep and reverent awe I replaced the candelabrum in its former position.
ex.ja: 深い畏敬の念を抱きながら、私は燭台を前あった場所に戻した。

note.ja: 北欧語 agi（恐れ）から。「畏怖・畏敬」。awful（もと「畏れ多い」→「ひどい」）、awesome（「畏れ多い」→「すごい」）も同じ。

en: A closed box in which the body of a dead person is placed for burial.
The eighth Lenormand card.
To place in a coffin.

coffin.ety: From Middle English coffyn, from Old Northern French cofin (“sarcophagus", earlier "basket, coffer”), from Latin cophinus (“basket”), a loanword from Ancient Greek κόφινος (kóphinos, “a basket”). Doublet of coffer. Displaced native Old English þrūh.

ex.en: The coffin was carried into the church.
ex.ja: 棺が教会に運び込まれた。

en: Possessing prominent and varied colors.
Interesting, multifaceted, energetic, distinctive.

ex.en: The picture is colorful in contrast with this one.
ex.ja: その絵はこの絵とは対照的にカラフルだ。

ex.en: Our garden is full of colorful flowers.
ex.ja: 庭園は色とりどりの花で溢れています。

ex.en: I saw a boy with colorful shoes.
ex.ja: カラフルな靴を履いた男の子を見たんだ。

note.ja: color（色）+ -ful。「色に満ちた」→「色彩豊かな」。

en: A small musical group.
An action composed of a sequence of simpler actions, especially a composite attacking move in a fighting game.
To perform a combo attack on.

ex.en: Good points: The pleasure of disposing of enemies with a variety of combos.
ex.ja: 良い所：様々なコンボで自由に敵を料理する楽しさ。

note.ja: combination（組み合わせ）の短縮。「組み合わせ・セット」。

en: Any far-left political ideology or philosophy advocating holding the production of resources collectively, especially by seizing it throu…
Any political social system that implements a communist political philosophy.

ex.ja: 私の生きているうちに共産主義が効力を持つことは無いだろう。

ex.en: Recently communism has extended its power.
ex.ja: 最近共産主義は拡大した。

ex.en: In communism, the means of production are owned by the state.
ex.ja: 共産主義の下では、生産手段は国有化される。

note.ja: com（共に）+ mun（務め）+ ism。財産を共有する主義 →「共産主義」。

en: One who conducts or leads; a guide; a director.
A person who conducts an orchestra, choir or other music ensemble; a professional whose occupation is conducting.

conductor.ety: Borrowed from Middle French conductour, from Old French conduitor, from Latin conductor.

ex.en: The famous conductor lives in New York.
ex.ja: その有名な指揮者はニューヨークに住んでいる。

ex.en: "Orange Cards" are available from the conductor.
ex.ja: オレンジカードは車掌が販売している。

ex.en: The conductor appeared on the stage.
ex.ja: 指揮者がステージに現れた。

note.ja: con（共に）+ duct（導く）+ or。導く人・もの →「指揮者・車掌・導体」。

en: Something that constrains; a restriction.
An irresistible force or compulsion.

constraint.ety: From Middle English constreynt, constreynte, from Old French constreinte, past participle of constreindre (“to constrain”), from Latin cōnstringō (corresponding to the past participle cōnstrictus).

ex.en: There are few legal constraints on the sale of firearms in the U.S.
ex.ja: 合衆国には小火器の販売に関する法律上の制約はほとんどない。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ strain（締める）+ t。きつく締めつけること →「制約・束縛」。

en: A bird, usually black, of the genus Corvus, having a strong conical beak, with projecting bristles; it has a harsh, croaking call.
Any of various dark-coloured nymphalid butterflies of the genus Euploea.
Dark black, the color of a crow; crow-black.
To use a crowbar, wedge, or other implement to attempt to open a surface by leveraging force on the opposite end of the tool to pry off t…

ex.ja: 屋根の上にいる鳥はからすです。

ex.ja: 烏は石炭のように黒い。

ex.en: Two crows are flying in the sky.
ex.ja: 二羽のからすが空を飛んでいます。

en: Having the power or quality of deciding a question or controversy; putting an end to contest or controversy; final; conclusive.
Decided; definite; incontrovertible.

decisive.ety: From Middle French décisif, equivalent to decide + -ive.

ex.en: I took a picture at the decisive moment.
ex.ja: 私は決定的瞬間を写真に撮った。

ex.en: Today's match was a decisive victory.
ex.ja: 今日の試合は、ボロ勝ちだったよ。

ex.en: Today's game was a decisive victory.
ex.ja: 今日の試合は、ボロ勝ちだったよ。

note.ja: decide（決める）+ -ive。de（離して）+ caedere（切る）。「切り離して決める」→「決定的な・決断力のある」。

en: That serves to decorate
That has no functional purpose.
A plant, tile, etc. intended for use as decoration.

decorative.ety: From Latin decorātus + -ive. Cognate with French décoratif.

ex.en: Do up the box with decorative tape.
ex.ja: その箱に飾りのテープをかけてください。

note.ja: decorate + -ive。「装飾的な」。

en: Explicitly defined.
Determining finally, conclusive, decisive.
a word, such as a definite article or demonstrative pronoun, that defines or limits something
an ordinary postage stamp that is part of a series of all denominations or is reprinted as needed to meet demand

ex.en: This book is the definitive guide to Japanese gardens.
ex.ja: この本は日本庭園についての決定版の案内書だ。

note.ja: definite（明確な）+ -ive。「決定的な」。define と同じ fin。

en: To put out of place; to disarrange.
To move something, or someone, especially to forcibly move people from their homeland.

ex.en: The villagers were displaced by the construction of a dam.
ex.ja: ダムの建設のため村民は立ち退かされた。

note.ja: dis（離して）+ place（置く）。「別の場所に置く」→「追い出す・取って代わる」。

en: A widespread disease that affects many humans in a population.
An occurrence of a disease or disorder in a human population at a frequency higher than that expected in a given time period; an episode …
Of, related to, or being an epidemic: a widespread outbreak of disease in humans.
Like an epidemic: widespread in a bad way.

epidemic.ety: From French épidémique, from épidémie, from Medieval Latin epidēmia, reanalysis of plural Late Latin epidēmia, from Ancient Greek ἐπιδήμιος (epidḗmios), from ἐπί (epí, “upon”) + δῆμος (dêmos, “people”). By surface analysis, epi- (“on”) + demic (“of the people”).

ex.en: An epidemic has broken out.
ex.ja: 疫病が発生した。

ex.en: A serious epidemic has broken out in Beijing.
ex.ja: 深刻な伝染病が北京で発生した。

ex.en: An epidemic disease broke out.
ex.ja: 伝染病が発生した。

note.ja: epi（上に・間に）+ dem（民衆）+ ic。民衆の間に広がる →「（病気の）流行・伝染病」。

en: Existence without end, infinite time.
Existence outside of time.

eternity.ety: From Middle English eternyte, from Old French eternité, from Latin aeternitās. Displaced native Old English ēcnes.

ex.en: I was kept waiting for an eternity.
ex.ja: 長い長い間私は待たされた。

ex.en: The door was closed for all eternity.
ex.ja: その扉は永久に閉ざされた。

ex.en: Eternity exists. It exists here...
ex.ja: 永遠はあるよ。ここにあるよ・・・。

note.ja: ラテン語 aeternus（永遠の）から。aevum（時代・永い時間）。「永遠」。eternal も同じ。

To destroy with an explosion.

ex.ja: そのニュースは彼の怒りを爆発させた。

ex.en: The time-bomb exploded with a loud noise.
ex.ja: 時限爆弾が大音響とともに爆発した。

en: The act of extracting or the condition of being extracted.
Something extracted, an extract, as from a plant or an organ of an animal etc.
