ex.en: Is there any other way besides extraction?
ex.ja: 抜歯しないで済ます方法はありますか。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ tract（引く）+ ion。引き出すこと →「抽出・抜歯・血統」。

en: Containing, composed of, or consisting of fat.
Sometimes, especially, containing excess fat.
A type of game played with marbles.

fatty.ety: From Middle English fatty, equivalent to fat + -y. Cognate with Saterland Frisian fattig (“fatty”), Dutch vettig (“fatty, greasy”), German Low German fettig (“fatty”), German fettig (“fatty”).

ex.en: Try not to eat too much fatty food.
ex.ja: 脂肪の多い食べ物を食べすぎないようにしなさい。

note.ja: fat（脂肪）+ -y。「脂肪の多い」。

en: Covered with filth; very dirty.
Obscene or offensive.
To make very dirty; to saturate something with dirt.
To cover in filth.

filthy.ety: From Middle English filthy, filthi, equivalent to filth + -y.

ex.en: Stop telling those filthy stories.
ex.ja: そんな汚らわしい話をするのはやめて。

ex.en: He was always filthy and looked like he wasn't given enough food.
ex.ja: いつもあかだらけで、食事も満足に与えられていない様子でした。

ex.en: Shut your filthy mouth.
ex.ja: 下品なことを言うな。

note.ja: filth（汚物）+ -y。filth は foul（汚い）と同じ祖先。「不潔な」。

en: A group of birds that have suddenly started up from undergrowth, trees, etc.
To cause to take flight from concealment.
To take suddenly to flight, especially from cover.
Smooth, even, aligned; not sticking out.
Wealthy or well off.
Suddenly and completely.

flush.ety: From Middle English flusshen, fluschen, of uncertain origin. Compare dialectal flusk (“to fly at, startle a bird out of the bush”) and flusker (“to flutter, fly irregularly”). Perhaps related to Middle English flasshen, flasschen, flaschen, see flash; or a Middle English blend of flowen (“to flow”) + guschen (“to gush”). Compare Saterland Frisian flutskje, German Low German flutschen, German flutschen.

ex.en: Pull the string and the water flushes.
ex.ja: ひもを引けば水が流れ出る。

ex.en: Those boys are in the first flush of youth.
ex.ja: あの少年たちは若さがあふれんばかりだ。

ex.en: The setting sun flushed the high roof.
ex.ja: 夕日は高い屋根を赤く染めた。

note.ja: 擬音的な語とされる。「（水が）どっと流れる」→「（トイレを）流す」、血がどっと上る →「赤面する」。

en: A receptacle in a church for holy water, especially one used in baptism.
A receptacle for lamp oil in a lamp.
To overlay (text) on the picture.

font.ety: From Old English font, an early borrowing from Latin fōns, fontis (“fountain”).

ex.en: In the font business you must never trust anybody!
ex.ja: フォント・ビジネスでは決して誰も信用してはいけないよ。

ex.en: Why do you use this font?
ex.ja: なんでこのフォント使ってるの？

ex.en: This font is hard to read.
ex.ja: このフォント、読みにくいなぁ。

note.ja: フランス語 fonte（鋳造）から。fondre（溶かす）。活字を鋳造したことから「書体・フォント」。fund（注ぐ）と同じ。「泉・源」の font はラテン語 fons からで別語。

en: A swimming event in which the contestants may choose any stroke.
The swimming stroke commonly referred to as the front crawl or the Australian crawl.
To improvise one's own style; to ad-lib.
To improvise one's dance moves; dance freely.

ex.en: She won the 100-meter freestyle.
ex.ja: 彼女は１００メートル自由形で優勝した。

note.ja: free（自由な）+ style（型）。「自由な型」→「自由形・フリースタイル」。

en: A hard gelatin made by boiling bones and hides, used in solution as an adhesive; or any sticky adhesive substance.
Anything that binds two things or people together.
To join or attach something using glue.
To cause something to adhere closely to; to cause to follow attentively.

glue.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *gleyH-
Proto-Indo-European *glóh₁ytn̥
Proto-Italic *gloiten
Latin glūten
Late Latin glūs
Old French glubor.
Middle English glew
English glue
From Middle English glew, glue, from Old French glu (“glue, birdlime”), from Late Latin glūs (stem glūt-), from Latin glūten. Related to clay.
Partially displaced native Old English līm (“glue”) and ġelīman (“to glue”) (whence modern lime).

ex.en: Some furniture is put together with glue.
ex.ja: 家具の中には、にかわづけで組み立てられているものもある。

ex.en: This glue does not adhere to plastic.
ex.ja: こののりはプラスチックには付かない。

ex.en: Glue the photograph to your application form.
ex.ja: 申し込み用紙に糊で写真を貼りなさい。

note.ja: ラテン語 glus（にかわ）から。「接着剤」。

en: grandfather.
Any elderly man, regardless of if he has, or whether one knows he has, grandchildren.

ex.en: My grandpa was born on Christmas Day.
ex.ja: 僕のおじいちゃん、クリスマスに生まれたんだよ。

ex.en: Let's visit my grandpa this weekend.
ex.ja: 週末におじいちゃんに会いに行こう。

ex.en: Grandpa lived until the age of 99.
ex.ja: 祖父は９９歳まで生きた。

note.ja: grandfather の幼児語。grand（一世代離れた）+ pa（パパ）。

en: Having a lot of body hair.
Having a lot of fur.

hairy.ety:
From Middle English hery, heeri, hary, equivalent to hair + -y. Compare Saterland Frisian hierich (“hairy”), West Frisian hierrich (“hairy”), Dutch harig (“hairy”), German Low German harig (“hairy”), German haarig (“hairy”), Swedish hårig (“hairy”), Icelandic hárugur (“hairy”). Compare also Old English hǣriht (“hairy”) and ġehǣre (“hairy”).
The sense "terrifying, scary" possibly results from a blend of hair-raising and scary.

ex.en: He has a hairy chest.
ex.ja: 彼は胸毛が多い。

ex.en: Tom does have hairy hands.
ex.ja: トムは、毛むくじゃらな手をしている。

ex.en: I'm scared of big, black, hairy tarantulas!
ex.ja: 大きい、黒い、もさもさトリクイグモが怖いんです！

note.ja: hair（毛）+ -y。「毛深い」→（俗）身の毛のよだつ →「危険な」。

en: The killing of one person by another, whether premeditated or unintentional.
A person who kills another.

homicide.ety: From Old French homicide, from Latin homicīda (“man-slayer”) and homicīdium (“manslaughter”).

ex.en: Tom was a homicide detective before he retired.
ex.ja: トムさんが退職するまで、殺人担当刑事でした。

note.ja: ラテン語 homo（人）+ caedere（殺す）。「人を殺すこと」→「殺人」。suicide（自分を殺す）、pesticide（害虫を殺すもの）と同じ -cide。

en: The passing of title to an estate upon death.
That which a person is entitled to inherit, by law or testament, such as the part of an estate (i.e., a portion).

inheritance.ety: Inherited from Middle English enheritaunce, inheritaunce, borrowed from Anglo-Norman, Old French enheritaunce, from enheriter. By surface analysis, inherit + -ance.

ex.en: I really wonder how much the inheritance tax will amount to.
ex.ja: いったいどれくらいの相続税を払うことになるんだろう。

ex.en: She claims the inheritance.
ex.ja: 彼女はその遺産を要求している。

note.ja: inherit（相続する）+ -ance。ラテン語 heres（相続人）。heir、heritage と同じ。「相続・遺産・遺伝」。

en: Characterized by or constituting (any kind of) irony.
Odd or coincidental; strange.

ironic.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin īrōnicus, from Ancient Greek εἰρωνικός (eirōnikós). Compare Middle French, ironique, equivalent to irony + -ic.

ex.en: It's ironic that the fire station burned down.
ex.ja: 消防署が火事で焼けてしまったとは皮肉なことだ。

note.ja: irony（皮肉）+ -ic。ギリシャ語 eirōneia（とぼけること）。「皮肉な」。

en: The bags and other containers that hold a traveller's belongings.
The contents of such containers.

luggage.ety: 1590s, lug (“to drag”) + -age, literally “that which is lugged, dragged around”. Compare baggage.

ex.en: Could you keep this luggage until 3 p.m.?
ex.ja: この荷物を午後３時まで預かっていただけますか。

ex.en: I'd like to send this luggage to Australia.
ex.ja: この荷物をオーストラリアに送りたいんですけど。

ex.en: Help me get this luggage into the truck.
ex.ja: この荷物をトラックに載せるの手伝って。

note.ja: lug（重いものを引きずる）+ -age。「引きずって運ぶもの」→「手荷物」。

en: An electromagnetic wave with wavelength between that of infrared light and radio waves.
To cook (something) in a microwave oven.

microwave.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *mey-der.?
Ancient Greek μῑκρός (mīkrós)
Ancient Greek μῑκρο- (mīkro-)lbor.
English micro-
English wave
English microwave
From micro- + wave.

ex.en: How long should I microwave this?
ex.ja: これ何分チンしたらいい？

ex.en: Let's go to the microwave together and heat these up.
ex.ja: 一緒にチンしてよ。

ex.en: Zap it in the microwave for thirty seconds.
ex.ja: 30秒、レンジでチンして。

note.ja: micro（小さい）+ wave（波）。「波長の短い電磁波」→「マイクロ波」→ それを使う「電子レンジ」。

en: To make (something) smaller or as small as possible; shrink; reduce.
To relegate or assign (something) to a less insignificant status; diminish.

ex.en: Wash your hands often to minimize the risk of illness.
ex.ja: 病気になる危険を最小限にするために、こまめに手を洗いなさい。

note.ja: min（小さい）+ im + ize。最小にする →「最小限にする・軽視する」。

en: A discrete and complete living thing, such as animal, plant, fungus or microorganism.
Something with many separate interdependent parts, seen as being like a living thing; an organic system.

organism.ety: First attested in 1701; from organ + -ism, from Ancient Greek ὄργανον (órganon, “a tool, instrument”), from Proto-Indo-European *werǵ- (“work”). Compare New Latin organismus.

ex.en: It is easy to consider man unique among living organisms.
ex.ja: 生物の中で人類が独特であると考えるのはたやすい。

ex.en: Man is a complex organism.
ex.ja: 人間は複雑な有機体だ。

ex.en: These creatures evolved from simpler organisms like jellyfish.
ex.ja: これらの生物はクラゲのようなもっと単純な有機体から進化した。

note.ja: organ（器官）+ -ism。「器官を持つもの」→「生物・有機体」。

en: To cause (someone or something) to be; to bring (someone or something) into existence; to produce or initiate a person or thing.
To come into existence; to have origin or beginning; to spring, be derived (from, with).

originate.ety: From Medieval Latin orīginātus, perfect passive participle of orīginō (“to begin, give rise to”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix) for more), from orīgō (orīgin- in compounds) + -ō. Compare Italian originare and Spanish originar. By surface analysis, origin + -ate.

ex.en: The concept of "zero" originated in India.
ex.ja: ゼロの概念はインドで発明されました。

ex.en: The custom originated in China.
ex.ja: その習慣は中国で始まった。

ex.en: That custom originated with the American Indians.
ex.ja: その習慣はアメリカンインディアンによってはじめられた。

note.ja: origin（起源）+ -ate。ラテン語 oriri（昇る・生じる）。「生じる・始まる」。orient（日の昇る方 → 東）も同じ。

en: An avoirdupois ounce, weighing ¹⁄₁₆ of an avoirdupois pound, or 28.349523125 grams.
A troy ounce, weighing ¹⁄₁₂ of a troy pound, or 480 grains, or 31.1034768 grams.

ounce.ety: From Middle English ounce, unce, from Middle French once, from Latin ū̆ncia (“Roman ounce, various similar units”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *óynos (“one”). Doublet of a, one, inch, uncia, onça, onza, oka, ouguiya, and awqiyyah.

ex.en: Cook about 12 ounces of rice.
ex.ja: お米2合炊いといて。

ex.en: An ounce of practice is worth a pound of precept.
ex.ja: 教訓よりも実行が大切。

ex.en: An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.
ex.ja: 予防は治療にまさる。

note.ja: ラテン語 uncia（12分の1）から。inch（1フィートの12分の1）と同じ語源。

en: To remove the skin or outer covering of.
To remove something from the outer or top layer of.
The skin or outer layer of a fruit, vegetable, etc.
The action of peeling away from a formation.

peel.ety: From Middle English pelen, from Old English pilian and Old French peler, pellier; both from Latin pilō, pilāre (“to remove hair from, depilate”), from pilus (“hair”). Doublet of pill.

ex.en: Peel the apple before you eat it.
ex.ja: リンゴを食べる前に皮をむきなさい。

ex.en: I'll peel an orange for you.
ex.ja: オレンジをむいてあげよう。

ex.en: Tom peeled the apple for Mary.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーにリンゴをむいてあげた。

note.ja: ラテン語 pilare（毛を抜く）から。「（皮を）むく」。

en: An informal social gathering, usually in a natural outdoor setting, to which the participants bring their own food and drink.
The meal eaten at such a gathering.
To take part in a picnic.

ex.en: The picnic was called off because of rain.
ex.ja: ピクニックは雨のために中止になった。

ex.en: We had lots of fun at the picnic.
ex.ja: ピクニックに行って、とても楽しかった。

ex.en: They went into the woods for a picnic.
ex.ja: 彼らは森へピクニックに出かけた。

note.ja: フランス語 pique-nique から。piquer（ついばむ）+ nique（つまらないもの）とされる。「各自が持ち寄る食事」→「ピクニック」。

en: A person who practices a profession or art, especially law or medicine.
One who does anything customarily or habitually.

practitioner.ety:

ex.en: He had been a practitioner of Aikido for seven years.
ex.ja: 彼は７年間、合気道をやっていた。

note.ja: practitian（実践者）+ -er。practice と同じ。「開業医・実践者」。

en: In a predominant manner. Most commonly or frequently by a large margin.

predominantly.ety:
Etymology tree
English predominant
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English predominantly
From predominant + -ly.

ex.en: The town's population is predominantly young.
ex.ja: その町の住民は大部分が若者だ。

note.ja: predominant（優勢な）+ -ly。pre + dominant。「主に」。

en: An original or primary word; a word not derived from another, as opposed to derivative.
A member of a primitive society.
Of or pertaining to the beginning or origin, or to early times; original; primordial; primeval; first.
Of or pertaining to or harking back to a former time; old-fashioned; characterized by simplicity.

primitive.ety: From Middle English primitif, from Old French primitif, from Latin prīmitīvus (“first or earliest of its kind”), from prīmus (“first”); see prime. Doublet of primitivo.

ex.en: Magic plays an important part in primitive society.
ex.ja: 呪術は未開社会においては重要な役割をもつ。

ex.en: This was quite primitive compared to that.
ex.ja: こちらはあちらに比べれば全く原始的だった。

ex.en: They used those primitive tools.
ex.ja: 彼らはああいった原始的な道具を使っていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 primitivus（最初の）から。primus（第一の）。「最初の段階の」→「原始的な」。prime、primary と同じ prim。

en: The careful governance and guidance of God (or another deity, nature, etc.).
A manifestation of divine care or direction; an instance of divine intervention.

providence.ety: From Middle English providence, from Anglo-Norman providence, Middle French providence, and their source, Latin prōvidentia (“providence, foresight”), from the present participle of prōvidēre (“to provide”). By surface analysis, provide + -ence. Displaced native Old English foresċēawung.

ex.en: Chance is a nickname for Providence.
ex.ja: 機会とは神意を表す一つのあだ名である。

note.ja: pro（前もって）+ vid（見る）+ ence。前もって見通すこと →「（神の）摂理・先見」。

en: A person who possesses, or appears to possess, extrasensory abilities such as clairvoyance, precognition and telepathy, as well as potent…
A person who supposedly contacts the dead; a medium.
Relating to or having the abilities of a psychic.
Relating to the psyche or mind, or to mental activity in general.

psychic.ety: From Ancient Greek ψυχικός (psukhikós, “relative to the soul, spirit, mind”). Earlier referred to as "psychical"; or from Ancient Greek ψυχή (psukhḗ, “soul, mind, psyche”). First appeared (as substantive) 1871 and first records 1895.

ex.en: Tom is psychic, but Mary isn't.
ex.ja: トムは超能力者なんだけど、メアリーは違うよ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 psyche（心・魂）から。psych + ic。→「霊能者・心霊の・精神の」。

en: An expert in the field of psychology.

psychologist.ety:

English psycholog(y)

From psycholog(y) + -ist.

ex.en: Tom is not an M.D. but a psychologist.
ex.ja: トムは医者じゃなくて心理学者だ。

ex.en: To my surprise, the noted psychologist was accused of a kidnapping.
ex.ja: 驚いたことに、その著名な心理学者は誘拐罪で告訴された。

ex.en: The prominent psychologist resembles my uncle in appearance.
ex.ja: その著名な心理学者は、見た目が私の叔父に似ている。

note.ja: psychology（心理学）+ -ist。ギリシャ語 psychē（魂・心）+ logia（学）。

en: Any small model of a person or animal able to be moved by strings or rods, or in the form of a glove.
A person, country, etc, controlled by another.
To control or manipulate like a puppet.

puppet.ety: From Middle English popet, probably from, though attested earlier than, Middle French poupette, diminutive of poupée (cf. also Medieval Latin *pupata), ultimately derived from Latin pupa (“doll, puppet; girl”). The nominal form first appears c. 1531, and the verbal form c. 1635. See also puppy.

ex.en: Do you happen to think that I'm your puppet?
ex.ja: ひょっとして私はあなたの操り人形だと思うの？

ex.en: A puppet does not know that it is being controlled.
ex.ja: 傀儡は操られている事を知らない。

ex.en: This puppet is my only friend.
ex.ja: このパペットは私の唯一の友達です。

note.ja: フランス語 poupette（小さな人形）から。ラテン語 pupa（女の子・人形）。puppy と同じ語源。

en: Of or relating to reproduction.
That reproduces.
A reproductive organism (especially such as in an insect).

ex.en: The penis is one of the male reproductive organs.
ex.ja: 陰茎は雄の生殖器のひとつ。

note.ja: reproduce（繁殖する）+ -ive。「生殖の」。

en: To regain or get back something.
To rescue (a creature).
A retrieval.
The return of a difficult ball.

retrieve.ety: Recorded in Middle English c. 1410 as retreve (altered to retrive in the 16th century; modern form is from c. 1650), from Middle French retruev-, stem of Old French retrover (“to find again”, modern retrouver), itself from re- (“again”) + trover (“to find”), probably from Vulgar Latin *tropāre (“to compose”).

ex.en: Your attempt to retrieve your password was not successful. Please try again.
ex.ja: パスワードを復旧する事はできませんでした。再試行してください。

ex.en: Recyclable waste is retrieved on the first and third Wednesday of the month.
ex.ja: 資源ごみは、第１水曜日と第３水曜日です。

note.ja: 古フランス語 retrover（再び見つける）から。re（再び）+ trouver（見つける）。「見つけ出して取り戻す」。

en: Any of a series of long curved bones occurring in 12 pairs in humans and other animals and extending from the spine to or toward the ster…
A part or piece, similar to a rib, and serving to shape or support something.
To shape, support, or provide something with a rib or ribs.
To tease or make fun of someone in a good-natured way.

rib.ety:
From Middle English rib, ribbe, from Old English ribb (“rib”), from Proto-West Germanic *ribi, from Proto-Germanic *ribją (“rib, reef”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rebʰ- (“arch, ceiling, cover”).
Cognate with Dutch rib (“rib”), Norwegian ribbe (“sparerib”), Norwegian ribben (“rib”), Low German ribbe (“rib”), German Rippe (“rib”), Old Norse rif (“rib, reef”), Serbo-Croatian rèbro (“rib”).
(wife or woman): In reference to the creation of Eve from Adam's rib in the Bible.

ex.en: He elbowed me in the ribs.
ex.ja: 彼はひじで私の脇腹をつついた。

note.ja: 古英語 ribb から。ドイツ語 Rippe と同じ。「肋骨」→ 肋骨のような骨組み。

en: Free from sin or guilt.
Moral and virtuous, perhaps to the point of sanctimony.
To make righteous; specifically, to justify religiously, to absolve from sin.

righteous.ety: From earlier rightuous, rightwose, rightwos, rightwise, from Middle English rightwise, rightwis, from Old English rihtwīs (“righteous, just”), corresponding to right + -wise (with assimilation of second element to -ous), or to right + wise (“way, manner”). Cognate with Scots richtwis (“righteous”), Old High German rehtwīsic (“righteous, just”), Icelandic réttvíss (“righteous, just”). Compare also thefteous, mighteous.

ex.en: He was filled with righteous anger.
ex.ja: 彼は正義の怒りに燃えていた。

note.ja: 古英語 rihtwīs ＝ right（正しい）+ wise（方法）。「正しい方法の」→「正しい・正義の」。

The characteristic of being a rivalrous good, such that it can be consumed or used by only one person at a time.

ex.en: The quarrel originated in rivalry between the two countries.
ex.ja: その争いの根源は二国間の対立関係にある。

note.ja: rival（競争相手）+ -ry。ラテン語 rivalis（同じ川を使う人）、rivus（小川）。「同じ水を奪い合う人」→「競争相手」。river と同系。

en: The rank, status, power or authority of a monarch.
People of royal rank, plus their families, treated as a group.

royalty.ety: From Middle English royaltee, roialtee, royalte, from Old French roialté, roiauté, realté (compare earlier Old French realted (“realm, kingdom”)), from Vulgar Latin *rēgālitās, from Latin rēgālis, equivalent to royal + -ty. Doublet of regality.

ex.en: Intel gets a huge royalty from the invention.
ex.ja: インテル社はその発明で膨大な特許料を得ている。

note.ja: royal（王の）+ -ty。「王族」→ 王に払う使用料から「印税」。

en: A food made of ground meat (or meat substitute) and seasoning, packed in a section of the animal's intestine, or in a similarly cylindric…
An individual item of this food.
To squeeze (something) tightly into in a rolled or sausage-like form.
To squeeze (something) into something tightly fitting.

sausage.ety:
Etymology tree
Anglo-Norman sausichebor.
Middle English sawsiche
English sausage
From late Middle English sawsiche, from Anglo-Norman sausiche (compare Norman saûciche), from Late Latin salsīcia (compare Sicilian sausizza, Spanish salchicha, Italian salsiccia), feminine of salsīcius (“seasoned with salt”), derivative of Latin salsus (“salted”), from sal (“salt”). More at salt. Doublet of saucisse. See also Sicilian sausizza. Displaced native Old English mearh.

ex.en: He dropped the sausage on the ground.
ex.ja: 彼はソーセージを地面に落とした。

ex.en: I wonder how sausage is made.
ex.ja: ソーセージって、どうやってできるんだろう。

ex.en: I wonder how sausages are made.
ex.ja: ソーセージって、どうやってできるんだろう。

note.ja: ラテン語 salsicia（塩漬けの）から。salsus（塩をした）。sauce、salad、salt と同じ sal。

en: The system that provides support to an organism, where in vertebrates it is internal and consists of bones and cartilage, and external in…
An anthropomorphic representation of a skeleton.

skeleton.ety: From New Latin sceleton, from Ancient Greek σκελετόν (skeletón), the neuter of σκελετός (skeletós, “dried up, withered, dried body, parched, mummy”), from σκέλλω (skéllō, “dry, dry up, make dry, parch”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kelh₁- (“to parch, wither”); compare Ancient Greek σκληρός (sklērós, “hard”).

ex.en: He's so thin that he looks like a skeleton.
ex.ja: 彼は骸骨のようにやせている。

ex.en: The poor old man was reduced to just a skeleton.
ex.ja: その貧しい老人は骨と皮だけになってしまった。

ex.en: He looks just like a skeleton.
ex.ja: 彼は骸骨のようにやせている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 skeletos（干からびた）から。「干からびた体」→「骸骨・骨格・骨組み」。

en: Of, pertaining to, or containing spice.
Of a flavor, provoking a burning sensation due to the presence of capsaicin or a similar chemical.

spicy.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *-yeti
Proto-Indo-European *spéḱyeti

From spic(e) + -y. First attested in the 16th century.

ex.en: I don't mind if it's hot and spicy.
ex.ja: 辛くてもへっちゃらだよ。

ex.en: "Do you like spicy food?" "I love it."
ex.ja: 「辛い食べ物って、好き？」「好き好き」

ex.en: I want to eat something that's not spicy.
ex.ja: 辛くないものが食べたい。

note.ja: ラテン語 species（種類→香辛料の品目）から。spec（見る）の仲間。→「香辛料の効いた・ぴりっとした」。

en: Tending to stick; able to adhere via the drying of a viscous substance.
Difficult, awkward.
A sticky note, such as a post-it note.
A small adhesive particle found in wastepaper.

sticky.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *(s)teyg-
Proto-Indo-European *stignéh₂-
Proto-Germanic *stikkōną
Proto-West Germanic *stikkōn
Old English stician
Middle English stiken
English stick
Proto-Indo-European *-kos
Proto-Germanic *-gaz
Proto-West Germanic *-g
Old English -iġ
Middle English -y
English -y
English sticky
From stick + -y.

ex.en: Japan is hot and sticky in summer.
ex.ja: 日本の夏は蒸し暑い。

ex.en: What's that sticky stuff on your shirt?
ex.ja: シャツについている、べとべとしたものは何ですか。

ex.en: City officials often have sticky fingers.
ex.ja: 市の議員だったらよくやっていることだよ。

note.ja: stick（くっつく）+ -y。「べとべとした」→ くっついて離れない →「厄介な」。

en: A bump left on the skin after having been stung.
A puncture made by an insect or arachnid in an attack, usually including the injection of venom.
To hurt, usually by introducing poison or a sharp point, or both.
To puncture with the stinger.

sting.ety: From Middle English styng, sting, stynge, stenge, from Old English sting, stincg (“a sting, stab, thrust made with a pointed instrument; the wound made by a stab or sting”), from Proto-Germanic *stingaz; possibly also from Old English stynġ, from Proto-Germanic *stungiz.

ex.en: I have a stinging pain here.
ex.ja: ここにひりひりする痛みがあります。

ex.en: Tom was stung by a bee.
ex.ja: トムは蜂に刺された。

ex.en: I was stung by a bee.
ex.ja: ハチに刺されちゃった。

note.ja: 古英語 stingan（刺す）から。「（ハチなどが）刺す」→ ひりひりさせる。stick（突き刺す）と同系。

en: In a sufficient manner; enough.
To a sufficient extent.

sufficiently.ety:
Etymology tree
English sufficient
Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der.
Proto-Germanic *līkąder.
Proto-Germanic *-līkaz
Proto-Germanic *-ê
Proto-Germanic *-līkê
Proto-West Germanic *-līkē
Old English -līċe
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English sufficiently
From sufficient + -ly.

ex.en: I think I understand you sufficiently well.
ex.ja: 君のことは充分理解しているつもりだよ。

ex.en: I haven't made up my mind sufficiently enough to agree with you.
ex.ja: まだ決心がつかないので同意できません。

ex.en: Even a cheap thing is sufficiently adequate.
ex.ja: 安物でも充分に満足です。

note.ja: sufficient（十分な）+ -ly。sub（下から）+ facere（作る）。「下から支えて足りるようにする」→「十分に」。suffice。

en: In a thankful manner; giving thanks.
fortunately, gratefully.

thankfully.ety: From Middle English thankfully, thankefully, þonkfulliche, from Old English þancfullīċe, equivalent to thankful + -ly.

ex.en: Thankfully, the medicine quickly started to take effect.
ex.ja: 幸い、薬の効果はすぐに現れた。

ex.en: Thankfully, the weather was nice and we were able to eat outside.
ex.ja: おかげさまで、天気にも恵まれ、外で食べることができました。

ex.en: Thankfully, the drive-thru was open 24/7.
ex.ja: 幸いにも、ドライブスルーは24時間365日開いていた。

note.ja: thankful + -ly。「ありがたいことに」。

en: A tiny woodland arachnid of the suborder Ixodida.
To make a clicking noise similar to the movement of the hands of an analog clock.
To make a tick or checkmark.

tick.ety: From Middle English tyke, teke, from Old English ticia (“parasitic animal, tick”), from Proto-West Germanic *tīkō, compare Dutch teek, German Zecke.

ex.en: The only sound to be heard was the ticking of the clock.
ex.ja: 聞こえる音は時計のカチカチという音だけだった。

ex.en: The clock is ticking.
ex.ja: 時計は時を刻んでいる。

ex.en: Mary has been really ticked off all morning, Tom, did something happen?
ex.ja: 朝からメアリーの虫の居所が悪いんだけどさ、トム、何かした？

note.ja: 「カチカチ」は擬音語。「チェックマーク」はその印から。「ダニ」は古英語 ticia からで別語。

en: Of or pertaining to a tutor; belonging to, or exercised by, a tutor.
A self-paced learning exercise; a lesson prepared so that a student can learn at their own speed or convenience.
An interactive class taught by a tutor to students at university or college, individually or in small groups.

tutorial.ety: The adjective is from tutor (noun) + -ial, ultimately from Latin tūtor (“watcher, protector, defender”). The noun is transferred from the adjective.

ex.en: He goes to a tutorial school three days a week.
ex.ja: 彼は週に三回塾に行く。

note.ja: tutor（個別指導者）+ -ial。ラテン語 tutor（保護者）。「個別指導」→ 使い方の「チュートリアル」。

en: The ordinal form of the number twenty.
A person or thing in the twentieth position.
One of twenty equal parts of a whole.

twentieth.ety:
From earlier twenteth, twentith, from Middle English twentithe, twentiþe, from Old English twēntigoþa. Equivalent to twenty + -eth.
Etymological notes
twentith, twenteth is the expected development from Middle English twentithe, but in time, the opaque twent- was replaced by a more transparent twenty-, resulting in modern twentieth (in the speech varieties this occurred in, the weak vowel in the final syllable of twenteth, twentith was clearly distinct from that in twenty); similar processes explain the modern pronunciation of thirtieth, fourtieth, etc. This analogy was assisted by synizetic p

ex.en: My birthday is on the twentieth of July.
ex.ja: 僕の誕生日は、７月２０日だよ。

ex.en: We arrived on the morning of the twentieth.
ex.ja: 私たちは２０日の朝に到着しました。

ex.en: The next meeting will be on October twentieth.
ex.ja: 次の会議は10月20日です。

note.ja: twenty + -eth（序数）。「20番目」。

en: Not pleasant.

unpleasant.ety: From Middle English unplesaunt, equivalent to un- + pleasant.

ex.en: How can you benefit by being so unpleasant?
ex.ja: そんなに突っけんどんにしてなんの得があるのか。

ex.en: The gas gives off a strong, unpleasant smell.
ex.ja: その気体は強い異臭を放つ。

ex.en: He has an unpleasant look in his eyes.
ex.ja: あの男は目つきが悪い。

note.ja: un（否定）+ pleasant（心地よい）。「不愉快な」。

en: Not connected or associated.
Not related by kinship.

unrelated.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *né
Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Germanic *un-
Proto-West Germanic *un-
Old English un-
Middle English un-
English un-
English related
English unrelated
From un- + related.

ex.en: May I ask you a totally unrelated question?
ex.ja: ちょっと全然関係ないこと聞いてもいい？

ex.en: May I ask you about something totally unrelated?
ex.ja: ちょっと全然関係ないこと聞いてもいい？

ex.en: Excuse me for the unrelated question.
ex.ja: つかぬことをお伺いします。

note.ja: un（否定）+ related（関係のある）。relate は re + latus（運ばれた）。

en: Not occupied; empty.
Blank.

vacant.ety: From Old French vacant, from Latin vacāns.

ex.en: He was standing there with a vacant look.
ex.ja: 彼はぽかんとした顔つきでそこに立っていた。

ex.en: There wasn't a single vacant seat in the hall.
ex.ja: ホールには空席は一つもなかった。

ex.en: The vacant lot is laid out as a park.
ex.ja: その空地は公園として設計されている。

note.ja: vac（空の）+ ant。空いている →「空いている・空席の・うつろな」。

en: An opening through which gases, especially air, can pass.
A small aperture.
To allow gases to escape.
To allow gases to escape from (a sealed space, container, etc.).

vent.ety: Partly from Middle French vent, from Latin ventus and partly from French éventer. Cognate with French vent and Spanish viento (“wind”) and ventana (“window”). Doublet of wind.

ex.en: He is apt to give vent to his feelings.
ex.ja: 彼は感情を表わしがちだ。

ex.en: He gave vent to his disappointment.
ex.ja: 彼は落胆した気持ちを表した。

note.ja: ラテン語 ventus（風）から。風の通り道 →「通気口・はけ口・（感情を）ぶちまける」。

en: Proximity; the state of being near.
Neighbourhood; nearby region; surrounding area.

vicinity.ety: From vicine + -ity, from Latin vīcīnitās (“neighborhood”) (compare French vicinité), from vīcīnus (“neighbor”) (compare French voisin), from vīcus (“village”).

ex.en: Kate's father is in the vicinity of the house.
ex.ja: ケイトのお父さんは家の周辺にいる。

ex.en: There are no hospitals in the vicinity of his house.
ex.ja: 彼の家の近くには病院がない。

note.ja: ラテン語 vicinus（近所の）から。vicus（村）。「近所・付近」。

en: To move without purpose or specified destination; often in search of livelihood.
To stray; stray from one's course; err.
An act or instance of wandering.
Deviation from a correct or normal value.

wander.ety: From Middle English wandren, from Old English wandrian (“to wander, roam, fly around, hover; change; stray, err”), from Proto-West Germanic *wandarōn (“to wander”), from *wandōn (“to turn, change”) + *-rōn (frequentative suffix). Cognate with Scots wander (“to wander”), German wandern (“to wander, roam, hike, migrate”), Dutch wandelen (“to wander, roam, hike, migrate”), Danish vandre (“to wander, roam, hike, migrate”), Swedish vandra (“to wander, hike”).

ex.en: Maybe I'll just wander off on my own.
ex.ja: ぶらりと一人旅でもしてくるかな。

ex.en: He has been wandering over Europe for months.
ex.ja: 彼は何ヶ月もヨーロッパを放浪してきた。

ex.en: We can't wander around the park at night.
ex.ja: 私たちは夜中に公園を散策するなんてできません。

note.ja: 古英語 wandrian（さまよう）から。wend（向かう）、wind（曲がる）と同系。

en: A governmental office or department in a monarchy which purchases, keeps, and cares for royal clothes.
The building housing such a department.
To act as a wardrobe department; to provide clothing or sets of clothes.
To order clothing online and return it for a refund after having worn it.

ex.en: She selected a blue dress from the wardrobe.
ex.ja: 彼女は洋服ダンスから青いドレスを選んだ。

ex.en: Put the clothes in the wardrobe.
ex.ja: 服は、洋服ダンスにおさめといて。

ex.en: Janet Jackson had a wardrobe malfunction.
ex.ja: ジャネット・ジャクソンは衣装の不具合で、見えてはいけないところが見えてしまった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 warderobe ＝ warder（守る）+ robe（衣服）。「衣服を守る所」→「洋服だんす・持ち衣装」。guard と同じ語源。

en: A moderate degree of heat; the sensation of being warm.
Friendliness, kindness or affection.

warmth.ety: From Middle English warmth, warmeth, wermþe, from Old English *wiermþu (“warmth”), from Proto-West Germanic *warmiþu (“warmness; warmth”), corresponding to warm + -th (abstract nominal suffix). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Waarmte (“warmth”), West Frisian waarmte (“warmth”), Dutch warmte (“warmth”), German Low German Warmte, Warmt (“warmth”).

ex.en: I can remember the warmth of her hands.
ex.ja: 私は彼女の手の温かさを覚えている。

ex.en: The warmth of their welcome made me happy.
ex.ja: 彼らの温かい歓迎を嬉しく思った。

ex.en: I can remember the warmth of his hands.
ex.ja: 彼の手のぬくもりが思い出されます。

note.ja: warm（暖かい）+ -th。「暖かさ・温かみ」。length、width と同じ -th。

en: A tool for felling trees or chopping wood etc. consisting of a heavy head flattened to a blade on one side, and a handle attached to it.
An ancient weapon consisting of a head that has one or two blades and a long handle.
To fell or chop with an axe.
To lay off, terminate or drastically reduce, especially in a rough or ruthless manner; to cancel.

axe.ety: From Middle English ax, axe, ex, from Old English æx (“axe”), from Proto-West Germanic *akusi (“axe”), from Proto-Germanic *akwisī (“axe”), probably from a Proto-Indo-European *h₂egʷsih₂ (“axe”), from *h₂eḱ- (“sharp, pointed”). Cognate with Scots aix (“axe”), Dutch aks (“axe”), German Axt (“axe”), Danish økse (“axe”), Faroese, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk øks (“axe”), Icelandic öxi (“axe”), Swedish yxa (“axe”), Latin ascia (“axe, mason's trowel”).

ex.en: Until now I've never used an axe.
ex.ja: 私は今まで斧を使った事がなかった。

ex.en: He's gonna get axed.
ex.ja: 彼はクビになるだろうね。

ex.en: She always has some axe to grind.
ex.ja: 彼女はいつも人に対してやいばをといでいます。

note.ja: 古英語 æx（斧）から。「斧」→「（予算などを）ばっさり削減する」。

en: An attractive woman.
A black femme lesbian.

belle.ety: From French belle (“beautiful”), from Latin bella.

ex.en: She used to be called the Belle of Asakusa.
ex.ja: 浅草小町と呼ばれたものだ。

note.ja: フランス語 belle（美しい女性）から。ラテン語 bellus（美しい）。beauty、embellish（飾る）と同じ。

en: A short report, especially one released through official channels to be immediately broadcast or publicized.
A time-sensitive news item or short news report.
To announce (something) by means of such a report or publication.
Introduces a fact (presumed to be obvious) of which the person addressed is ostensibly not aware.

bulletin.ety: Borrowed from French bulletin. By surface analysis, bull (“ball”) + -et (“diminutive”) + -in (“diminutive”).

ex.en: We can get a weather bulletin every day.
ex.ja: 私達は毎日天気予報を知ることができる。

ex.en: Was there a need to stream that news bulletin?
ex.ja: 速報で流す必要あったか？

ex.en: Was there a need to air that news bulletin?
ex.ja: 速報で流す必要あったか？

note.ja: イタリア語 bullettino（小さな文書）から。bulla（封印・文書）。bill（請求書）と同じ語源。

en: Of, or pertaining to, capitalism.
Supporting or endorsing capitalism.
The owner of a considerable amount of capital; a wealthy person.
Someone whose wealth (capital) is invested in business ventures in order to return a profit.
